findings.title: Rebuild aborts and stays broken on any stale human decision because DecisionError is re-raised even in replay mode
findings.evidence: In apply(), `except DecisionError: raise` comes before the generic `except Exception` whose comment says a stale decision must never break a rebuild (decisions.py:88-94). _need(), _op_merge and _op_add_edge ('cannot link an entity to itself') all raise DecisionError, and rebuild() calls apply_all with no guard. Reproduced two ways. First, an add_edge followed by a merge of the same pair aborts rebuild. Second, a decision on claim keys plus lowered merge thresholds (which is what switching to bge-m3 does) gives 'entity claim:... not found'.
findings.scenario: After the documented `rhz settings set embedder bge-m3` + `rhz rebuild` on a curated library, the rebuild aborts with a traceback that names an entity, not a decision. The Settings rebuild button silently does nothing, and DELETE /decision enqueues a rebuild that fails, so revokes never take effect. The library stays intact through rollback but can no longer be recomputed.
findings.fix: In apply(), when strict is False, catch DecisionError, log it with d.id, return False, and collect the skipped ids into the rebuild summary or a KV 'rebuild_warnings' the UI can show. Make _op_add_edge and _op_edge_status treat src==dst after redirect resolution as a no-op. Add a regression test that runs add_edge then merge of the same pair and expects rebuild to succeed.

findings.title: A corrected re-export never supersedes the old one, and there is no way to withdraw a paper or reject a hallucinated entity
findings.evidence: Nothing ever sets Extraction.is_current=False, and grep finds no assignment. rebuild replays every current extraction. There is no DELETE route other than /decision, no CLI retract command, and no entity-level reject op. Read paths filter only edge status or `!= candidate`. A repro shows that after rejecting every edge of dataset:GSE999002, search, data and recall still return it first, and its review card stays unsuspended.
findings.scenario: Claude hallucinates an accession or claim, and the user corrects it in chat and re-exports. Both exports stay current, the wrong dataset keeps being pushed back through recall and review cards, and it reappears after every rebuild. The only fix is manual SQL.
findings.fix: Add a `retract` HumanDecision (undoable through the existing revoke) that flips is_current on a work's extractions and enqueues a rebuild. Expose it as `rhz retract`, POST /work/{key}/retract and a paper-card button, and keep it off MCP. Add `replace: bool` to /ingest, the CLI and rhz_ingest, and return existing_exports when the work already has current rxf rows. Add a `reject_entity` op, and filter rejected entities through one shared visibility predicate in search, recall, datasets, views, vocab, FTS/VECTORS fill and due_cards. Also make decisions replay tolerant (see D1).

findings.title: Rebuild and other jobs hold one SQLite write transaction for minutes to hours; 'read' endpoints write, so the UI, MCP and inbox fail with 'database is locked'
findings.evidence: rebuild() deletes Edge, Embedding, Alias, Work and Entity first, re-materialises everything, and commits only when run_next's session_scope exits. retro_tag and nightly also run as one transaction. GET paths write: touch() on entity and topic views, and the VectorCache merge in embed_texts for new search queries. So once the 30 s busy timeout is reached they return 500. ingest_file moves files that hit 'database is locked' into error/, and a test pins that behaviour. Every revoke enqueues a full rebuild, enqueue never deduplicates, and recover_stale_jobs requeues an interrupted rebuild at startup. After a model switch the rebuild runs for hours on CPU, and because the cache writes roll back on a kill it restarts from zero.
findings.scenario: With about 2,000 papers the user revokes one merge, or clicks 重算 after switching to bge-m3. For minutes or hours every entity card, new search and MCP call hangs 30 s and then errors, and inbox drops land in error/ with a misleading 'fix the fields' report. Closing the laptop kills the job, and it restarts from zero at the next launch.
findings.fix: (1) Make the read paths write-free. embed_texts(persist=False) for query vectors plus an in-process LRU; touch() buffered in memory and flushed by the worker in a short transaction with a short busy_timeout. WAL readers then never block. (2) Keep rebuild atomic, but pre-embed texts and cache reranker scores in committed batches before the destructive deletes, so the locked phase only does DB work and a restart is cheap. (3) Coalesce rebuild jobs: reuse a queued one rather than enqueue another. (4) Expose the running job via GET /jobs/active, show a banner, and return 503 with Retry-After from write endpoints during long jobs. (5) Leave inbox files that hit a lock in place and retry them on a periodic rescan. (6) Have `rhz rebuild` enqueue through HTTP when the app is up.

findings.title: Rebuild recycles and reshuffles numeric entity ids, which the UI, CLI and MCP use as handles
findings.evidence: Entity.id is a plain integer PK. rebuild deletes and recreates rows in extraction order, and Graph.create lets SQLite pick rowids. A repro with a user topic plus a merge changed 29/29 ids, 28 of them now pointing at a different entity. rhz_related accepts only an int id, UI URLs are entity/<id>, and ReviewItem ids are recycled too, so a stale rhz_decide(item_id) can resolve a different pair. test_rebuild_is_deterministic compares only key sets.
findings.scenario: Claude holds id 812 from an earlier rhz_search. The user clicks 重算 or revokes a decision, and Claude's next rhz_related(812) silently reasons about a different paper. A stale review page can persist a wrong merge.
findings.fix: Snapshot {key: id} (and pending ReviewItem dedupe_key: id) before the deletes, and have Graph.create and Graph.queue assign the old id or the next explicit id from max+1. No migration is needed. Extend the determinism test to compare the full key→id map. Make MCP key-first: rhz_related(entity: str), with docstrings saying keys are the durable handles.

findings.title: Every rebuild, revoke and migration writes a full database copy that is never pruned, and a failed backup fails the rebuild job
findings.evidence: backup_database writes rhizome-{tag}-{ts}.db, and nothing lists or deletes backups. rebuild defaults to backup=True, and both triggers (revoke at app.py:380 and the Settings button) send {}. enqueue does not deduplicate, so five revokes make five full copies. Embedding and VectorCache store each vector twice, so a copy runs to hundreds of MB at 5k papers. Orphaned .tmp files from a disk-full failure persist. move_data_dir copies backups/ too. A failed backup marks the job failed, and the UI never polls job status.
findings.scenario: Day 30: %APPDATA%\Rhizome\backups (a roaming profile on the system drive) holds dozens of near-identical multi-hundred-MB copies. Once the disk fills, every rebuild fails at the backup step, so revokes and model switches never take effect, and nothing is shown to the user.
findings.fix: Add prune_backups after every write: keep the newest 3 pre-rebuild, the newest ~5 pre-<rev>, and all manual backups, and delete stray *.tmp. Skip the pre-rebuild backup when one from the last few minutes exists, or at least make it best-effort with a warning. Coalesce queued rebuilds. Show backup count, size and location in Settings and `rhz diag`.

findings.title: No scheduled or off-disk backup: the promise that 'L0 alone can rebuild everything' is false, and all human decisions and FSRS history live only in rhizome.db
findings.evidence: backup_database copies only rhizome.db, into data_dir/backups on the same disk, and is called only by manual `rhz backup`, pre-migration and pre-rebuild. The nightly job never backs up. rebuild reads only L1 rows and never raw/. HumanDecision, user topics, ReviewLog and KV tuning are not in L0. A scratch test that re-ingested raw/ into a fresh dir lost all decisions and the user topic, and reset FSRS state. The design doc promises a daily DB copy plus L0 syncing, and implementation.zh.md marks backup ✅.
findings.scenario: The user follows the docs and syncs only raw/ to a cloud drive. The SSD dies, or rhizome.db is corrupted after a crash, and months of merges, rejections, topic curation and review history are gone. `rhz rebuild` on a fresh DB reports extractions: 0.
findings.fix: (1) Take a nightly backup_database(tag='daily') with rotation, triggered at startup if the last one is older than 20 h. Make backup_dir configurable so it can sit outside data_dir (a closed copy is safe in a cloud folder; the live WAL DB is not). Show the last backup time. (2) Append decisions (and optionally ReviewLog grades) to raw/decisions/*.jsonl after each commit, and add an idempotent restore-decisions replay. (3) Correct README and design.zh.md to say exactly what L0 covers. (4) Add `rhz reingest --from-raw` later (see D30).

findings.title: synchronous=NORMAL and un-fsynced raw files: after a power loss a paper can disappear from the DB while its export already sits in inbox/done/
findings.evidence: WAL runs with synchronous=NORMAL and there is no checkpoint or fsync anywhere. rawstore.put writes <sha>.tmp and renames it without fsync, and `if not p.exists()` means a truncated L0 file is never rewritten. ingest commits, then moves the file to done/, and done/ is never rescanned.
findings.scenario: A hard power cut or BSOD within seconds of '已存入'. The last ingest rolls back, its export is already in done/, and the raw/ copy may be 0 bytes. Nothing tells the user.
findings.fix: Use PRAGMA synchronous=FULL on the read-write engine; commits are few. In rawstore.put, use mkstemp in the same dir, write, flush+fsync, then os.replace, so each process also gets a unique tmp name. Skip the directory fsync on Windows. Add a `rhz diag` check for missing or 0-byte raw files and stray .tmp files instead of a startup scan.

findings.title: RHIZOME_DATA_DIR pinned into claude_desktop_config.json goes stale after a library move, so Claude's MCP silently writes to the abandoned copy
findings.evidence: claude_desktop_snippet writes env.RHIZOME_DATA_DIR whenever data_dir is not the platform default, and env takes precedence over the location.json pointer. move_data_dir only rewrites the pointer and never touches or flags Claude's config, and it deletes nothing, so the old folder keeps working. connect() reads the old dir's token and server.json, fails the probes, and falls back to LocalClient on the old copy. The value is also unresolved, so a relative env path is copied verbatim. release.yml and test_system.py exercise exactly this path. In portable mode the snippet's command is an absolute exe path as well.
findings.scenario: The user moves the library to D:\研究\Rhizome, connects Claude Desktop, and later moves it again or back to the default. From then on every '存入 Rhizome' lands in the old library, rhz_recall answers from frozen data, and if the user deletes the old folder the MCP process recreates an empty one there.
findings.fix: Stop emitting env for pointer and portable resolution, since `rhz.exe mcp` resolves both itself. Emit it only when the process got an explicit RHIZOME_DATA_DIR (resolved) and is not portable. In move_data_dir and at app startup, find an existing mcpServers.rhizome entry carrying env.RHIZOME_DATA_DIR, remove or rewrite it (keeping a .bak), and return claude_config_updated so the UI says to restart Claude. Add a portable note: changing the drive letter requires re-running Claude setup. Add a test: install on a custom dir, move, and check the config no longer names the old path.

findings.title: move_data_dir has no safe window: the running app keeps writing to the old dir until restart, the copy is synchronous and non-atomic, and an active RHIZOME_DATA_DIR override makes the move a no-op
findings.evidence: After the copy the server keeps its Settings, worker and inbox watcher on the old dir. The UI only shows 请重启 and has no restart button. A CLI or MCP process started after the move follows the pointer to the new dir; the token is not copied, so it runs in LocalClient mode. That gives two writers on two libraries. The copy runs inside the request with no progress indicator. An interrupted copy leaves a non-empty folder that every retry refuses, and an OSError gives an unmapped 500. An env RHIZOME_DATA_DIR overrides the pointer, so the UI reports success but the restart changes nothing.
findings.scenario: The user moves the library and keeps working for an hour. Inbox papers go into the old dir while Claude's new MCP process writes into the new dir. After the restart the two inbox papers are 'missing'.
findings.fix: Once the move succeeds, set app.state.moved_to. Make the writable guard return 409 '资料库已迁移，请重启', have /health report read_only, stop the watcher and worker, and offer a 立即重启 button (Tauri app.restart). Copy into <target>.rhizome-moving and rename it at the end, removing it on failure, and map OSError to 422. Refuse the move up front when data_dir comes from env or --data-dir, and expose data_dir_source in /system.

findings.title: A location.json pointer to an unavailable target either crashes startup or silently creates a new empty library, with no recovery UI
findings.evidence: default_data_dir returns the pointer target unchecked, and ensure_dirs runs mkdir(parents=True) on it before init_db. An unmounted drive raises FileNotFoundError, so the sidecar exits with a traceback. A creatable path (a re-lettered drive, a deleted or renamed folder, %APPDATA% copied to a new PC) gets a brand-new empty rhizome.db, and settings fall back to defaults. Reproduced: `rhz search GRN` printed 'No results.' with exit 0 and created a fresh DB. The only reset is deleting location.json by hand.
findings.scenario: The library is on a USB SSD and the user launches without it: a traceback. Or the drive letter now belongs to another disk: an empty library appears, MCP ingests go into it, and when the real drive returns there are two diverged libraries.
findings.fix: When the path comes from the pointer and Path(target).is_dir() is false, raise LibraryNotFound. Never mkdir a pointer target. In the CLI, MCP and rhz_entry, print a bilingual one-liner and exit with a distinct code. On that code, main.rs offers Retry / Use default (deleting location.json). Add `rhz data-dir --reset`. Add a test that a missing pointer target raises and creates nothing.

findings.title: The Settings hint recommends putting the WAL SQLite library in 'a synced folder', with no guard against OneDrive, network or removable targets
findings.evidence: move_hint suggests 'another drive or a synced folder'. move_data_dir checks only that the path is absolute and the folder is empty or holds a library. Backups live inside data_dir, so they sync along with the live DB and -wal file.
findings.scenario: The user moves the library into OneDrive or 坚果云 and opens it from a second PC. The result is lock errors, 'rhizome.db-conflict' copies or a torn image, and the only backups are in the same synced folder.
findings.fix: Rewrite the hint in both locales: no cloud-sync or network folder; to sync, sync the backup files. Have move_data_dir return warnings for UNC paths, DRIVE_REMOTE or DRIVE_REMOVABLE, and paths under OneDrive, Dropbox, 坚果云 or 百度网盘, and have the UI confirm. Run PRAGMA quick_check before switching to an existing library. Allow backups_dir outside data_dir.

findings.title: HPC snapshot: FTS5 trigram query is unguarded (old libsqlite3 crashes search) and there is no schema-revision check
findings.evidence: has_fts() only looks at sqlite_master, so on SQLite <3.34 or without FTS5, keyword_ids raises 'no such tokenizer: trigram' instead of falling back to the alias LIKE path. With pretty_exceptions off the user gets a raw traceback. connect(snapshot=...) never compares the snapshot's alembic revision with the code's head.
findings.scenario: On an EL8 login node with a system-SQLite Python, `rhz --snapshot ... recall --from-file analysis.py` gives a traceback. Later a laptop on 0.2 ships a 0002 snapshot to an old cluster clone, which fails with 'no such column'.
findings.fix: Wrap the FTS query in try/except OperationalError: log once with sqlite3.sqlite_version and fall through to the LIKE branch. In snapshot mode compare current_revision with head, and print a bilingual message naming both when they differ. Document the SQLite ≥3.34 requirement and print the version in `rhz diag`. Add a test that monkeypatches the FTS query to raise.

findings.title: Snapshots inherit WAL mode, so opening them with mode=ro fails in a read-only directory and is fragile on NFS/Lustre
findings.evidence: copy_sqlite uses the backup API, which keeps header bytes 18/19 = 2,2 (WAL). sqlite_ro_uri is `mode=ro` without immutable. Running as uid nobody in a 0555 dir gives 'attempt to write a readonly database'; with immutable=1 the open works. In writable dirs every read leaves -shm and -wal files behind. The read-only engine also gets a 5 s busy timeout.
findings.scenario: The user syncs a snapshot into a group-read-only project dir or a read-only bind mount, and `rhz --snapshot ...` cannot open the file at all. On multi-node NFS, batch jobs contend on the -shm lock.
findings.fix: In make_snapshot (not copy_sqlite, which is shared with backups), copy to a temp file, run `PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE` (optionally VACUUM), close it, then os.replace. In the read-only branch of make_engine, append `&immutable=1` only when the header says rollback journal (bytes 18-19 == 1,1), so WAL files such as the live DB are never opened immutable, and pass timeout=30. Add a test that asserts the header bytes and opens the file from a chmod 0555 dir.

findings.title: vector_cache grows without bound (every query, every entity text, every past model) and gets copied into every backup, snapshot and sync
findings.evidence: embed_texts merges a VectorCache row for every uncached text: every search, every rhz_recall context, every canonicalize probe, and every entity text, which duplicates the Embedding table. rebuild deletes Embedding but never VectorCache, so rows for old models remain after a hashing→bge-m3 switch. Each row stores only sha+vec, not plaintext. Nothing VACUUMs. Snapshots are full page copies, and sync scps the whole file with no pruning.
findings.scenario: At 5,000 papers the dead rows for old models alone are ~150 MB. Every backup carries roughly twice the vectors it needs, and each `rhz sync` over a 2FA SSH session pushes hundreds of MB to 1 GB, so the user stops syncing.
findings.fix: Pass embed_texts(persist=False) from search, recall and probes, using an in-process LRU instead. During rebuild or `rhz gc`, delete vector_cache rows with model != current and rows whose text_sha matches no current entity text, then VACUUM from an explicit maintenance action. In make_snapshot, use VACUUM INTO a temp file, delete vector_cache and other-model embeddings plus access_log and job rows, set journal_mode=DELETE, VACUUM, and then ship the file. Add a test that a snapshot contains 0 vector_cache rows.

findings.title: FTS rows drift from aliases: add_alias and auto-merge or NLI merges never reindex, and rebuild reproduces the drift
findings.evidence: Alias additions in _op_add_alias, resolve_free auto-merge and the NLI merge never refresh entity_fts. rebuild replays through the same paths, so the drift survives it. In a reproduction, with 260 entities matching a CJK trigram query, FTS returns 200 rows, the LIKE fallback is skipped, and the aliased entity is missing entirely.
findings.scenario: A Chinese variant name exported from a chat auto-merges into an English entity. Keyword search for that Chinese name ranks low or misses it, permanently.
findings.fix: Make Graph.add_alias return whether it inserted, and call a split-out _refresh_fts(e) when it did. Pass index=False from create, merge and materialize's work-alias block, which already reindex. Add Alembic 0002 to re-derive every FTS row. Add an invariant test that every alias appears in its FTS text after add_alias, auto-merge and rebuild. Reuse the same body in snapshot.py.

findings.title: Schema migrations are neither atomic nor serialised across processes: a crash mid-migration bricks every start, and concurrent app and MCP starts race
findings.evidence: init_db reads current_revision without a lock, backs up, then runs command.upgrade inside engine.begin(). pysqlite issues no BEGIN before DDL, so CREATE and ALTER statements and batch-mode table copies autocommit while alembic_version rolls back. A CREATE TABLE inside engine.begin() was verified to survive a rollback. Three concurrent init_db calls on an empty dir failed with 'table access_log already exists' in 3 of 5 runs. The connect listener sets foreign_keys=ON, which makes batch drops of entity cascade-delete.
findings.scenario: 0.2 ships migration 0002. A large library migrates at first launch and the window is closed after the 90 s timeout, or taskkill runs, or the laptop dies. The DB is left with half the DDL applied and an old revision, every later start fails with 'already exists', and each retry writes another full backup. Or Claude Desktop's MCP races the app and crashes.
findings.fix: Use a dedicated migration engine (NullPool, isolation_level=None, PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF) and issue BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Re-read the revision inside the lock and return if it is already head. Take the backup inside the lock. Pass the connection via cfg.attributes, run PRAGMA foreign_key_check before COMMIT, and set a long busy_timeout. Leave make_engine unchanged. Add tests: a failing fake 0002 leaves the schema unchanged; two processes produce exactly one backup and both succeed.

findings.title: A newer or downgraded DB is not detected: init_db writes a misleading pre-backup and then dies with a raw Alembic error, and the installer allows downgrades
findings.evidence: `if cur != head` backs up as 'pre-<head>' before upgrade raises "Can't locate revision", and it does this on every start, piling up copies. The 'backed up to' line goes only to rhizome.log, while the user sees the English traceback tail. Tauri's allowDowngrades defaults to true. Latent until 0002 ships.
findings.scenario: The user installs 0.2, hits a bug and reinstalls 0.1.2. The window shows 'backend stopped' with a traceback and no pointer to the right backup, and `rhz` and MCP fail the same way.
findings.fix: Before any backup, check whether ScriptDirectory knows `cur`. If not, raise SchemaTooNew without writing a backup. Write data_dir/schema.json with the app_version after each upgrade, and have the message name it plus the backups dir. Have the CLI and MCP print the message without a traceback. Optionally set allowDowngrades=false. Add a test that stamps '9999', asserts the error, and checks backups/ stays empty. Startup timeout handling is in L1.

findings.title: The startup watchdog gives up for good at 90 s, and once the first TCP accept succeeds it stops watching the backend
findings.evidence: The poll thread shows '后台服务已退出' when the child exits or when 90 s pass, even if the child is still alive (slow migration, AV scan), and it never re-polls. After navigate it returns, so a later backend death leaves every page showing the generic 'common.error'.
findings.scenario: The first launch after an upgrade on an AV-scanned HDD takes 100 s. The user sees a false 'stopped' page, closes the window, kills the migration and loops. Or Defender quarantines rhz.exe mid-session and every page says 出错了, with no hint that a restart is needed.
findings.fix: When the timeout passes and the child is alive, show a soft 'still starting / 正在升级，请勿关闭' notice and keep polling. Never kill the child on timeout. After navigate, keep checking try_wait every ~2 s, and on exit call show_error with the log tail and '请关闭并重新打开'. Have req() map a fetch TypeError to ApiError(0) and show 'backend unreachable'.

findings.title: There is no restore path for the backups the app makes, and a manual restore next to a live -wal file corrupts the DB
findings.evidence: Only `rhz backup` exists, with no restore. The sidecar is TerminateProcess'd on exit, so no clean close checkpoints and deletes -wal, and an MCP process often keeps the DB open.
findings.scenario: After a failed 0.2 migration or a downgrade, the user copies rhizome-pre-0002.db over rhizome.db in Explorer. The stale -wal replays into it and the result is 'database disk image is malformed'.
findings.fix: Add `rhz restore <backup>`. It opens the live DB with timeout=0 and BEGIN EXCLUSIVE, aborts with 'close the app and Claude Desktop' if busy, checks integrity and a known revision, takes a pre-restore backup, then runs sqlite3 backup(source=backup → live) so no files are swapped. List backups with their revisions in Settings. Point the SchemaTooNew message (U2) at it.

findings.title: Review-card identity is sha(entity_key+q) with no reconciliation: cards duplicate after merge+rebuild or a language switch, or are orphaned after auto-merge, and stale retro_tag items return 422
findings.evidence: Graph.merge rewrites entity_key but not the card id, so the next rebuild inserts a fresh 'new' duplicate. Template q is rendered in the current UI language, and a changed local-LLM model changes q, so both produce new ids. Auto-merge records no redirect, so after a model or threshold change a card's key may no longer exist: due_cards serves it with entity_name None, and a duplicate appears under the surviving key. rebuild never touches ReviewCard, AccessLog or pending retro_tag/synthesis items. Resolving a stale retro_tag item as about/applicable_to raises 'entity not found' (422), and Review.tsx act() has no catch.
findings.scenario: After switching to bge-m3 and rebuilding, or merging methods, or toggling the language, the daily deck fills with nameless or duplicated cards that have no FSRS history, and the user's priority-10 idea cards fork.
findings.fix: In Graph.merge, re-key each card to card_id(into.key, q). On collision, keep the card with review history, move its ReviewLog rows, and delete the other. Use slot-based ids for generated cards (sha(entity_key+'generated')) and update q in place. At the end of rebuild, merge orphan cards into live siblings with the same q (copying FSRS state and ReviewLog), suspend the rest, delete orphan access_log rows, and mark pending items whose keys are gone as obsolete. Make review.resolve mark an item obsolete when its keys are missing. Ship a one-off migration to clean up existing duplicates.

findings.title: The in-process vector index copies the whole matrix on every new entity (np.vstack under the lock), which makes rebuild O(N²)
findings.evidence: upsert runs np.append on ids and types and np.vstack on mat for each unseen id; remove does a full mask copy. Measured: ~43 ms at 30k×1024 and ~235 ms at 150k. Both run inside the ingest or rebuild write transaction. After VECTORS.clear(), the first knn reloads the cache and every later entity copies the growing matrix again.
findings.scenario: At 5k+ papers each ingest spends seconds copying memory inside the write lock, and a rebuild spends extra minutes in vstack with a 2× peak memory spike.
findings.fix: Use a preallocated buffer with capacity doubling and a logical length (mat[n]=vec), or collect pending rows and fold them in lazily in get(). During rebuild, suspend in-place maintenance and do one bulk load afterwards. Add a test that 1,000 upserts do not copy the matrix.

findings.title: The embedding model is a per-process setting, not a property of the library: switching with the app open gives empty knn, silent duplicate entities, a mixed-model index, and partial HPC snapshots
findings.evidence: get_settings() is cached for the life of the process. `rhz settings set embedder` only writes the file, and `rhz rebuild` runs in the CLI process. knn filters Embedding.model == get_embedder().name and silently returns [] when no rows or dims match. PATCH /settings switches the embedder immediately with no rebuild gating; only a hint string mentions it. reindex writes only the current model, so after a switch an HPC snapshot has hashing vectors only for older entities. resolve_free then finds no merge candidates.
findings.scenario: The user follows the docs while Rhizome is open, or picks bge-m3 in Settings and forgets to rebuild. Searches become keyword-only, recall returns nothing, and every afternoon ingest creates duplicate datasets, methods and topics without any warning.
findings.fix: Record kv['embedding_model'] in the same transaction where rebuild rewrites Embedding (and on first ingest). knn and reindex compare it with the process's model: on a mismatch, reload settings, reset models and retry once, then raise a clear error. Never return [] silently and never write mixed vectors. Have PATCH /settings return rebuild_required with an asset count, have the UI confirm and then run the rebuild job, and keep a persistent index_stale banner plus an MCP warning. Route `rhz settings set` and `rhz rebuild` through HTTP when the app is up. Make make_snapshot warn about, or fill in, missing hashing coverage.

findings.title: CLI commands bypass a running app: `rhz settings set` is invisible to it and later overwritten by PATCH, and rebuild, nightly and watch run as second writers next to the app's worker and watcher
findings.evidence: PATCH merges into the stale cached model and writes the whole model back, which reverts CLI edits. rebuild, nightly, review and watch never consult connect(). `rhz nightly` drains the app's whole job queue with run_all, and `rhz watch` adds a second observer on the same inbox. The README advertises both.
findings.scenario: With the app open: `rhz settings set embedder bge-m3`, then a toggle in the UI reverts it. `rhz rebuild` locks the app's worker out, and two inbox watchers race on the same file.
findings.fix: When a server is live: send `settings set` as PATCH with only the changed key; turn rebuild and nightly into POST /jobs plus polling; send review through /cards/*; refuse `rhz watch` with a message. Make PATCH merge against a fresh load_settings so direct file edits are not lost. Have `rhz nightly` run only the job it enqueued.

findings.title: Following the documented bge-m3 switch breaks the installed desktop app: the frozen build has no sentence-transformers and shares settings.json with the pip CLI
findings.evidence: registry imports hf models without a guard, and rhz.spec excludes torch, transformers and sentence_transformers. The pip CLI and the frozen app read the same %APPDATA% settings.
findings.scenario: The user pip-installs the backend to get bge-m3 and runs the documented commands. In the app every search, recall and ingest now returns 500, the inbox moves every RXF to error/, and MCP fails, while browsing looks healthy. Builtin can still be re-selected in Settings, but nothing explains the failure.
findings.fix: Have the registry detect that the model cannot be imported. Record a model_unavailable state, surface it in /system and MCP, and show a banner with a 'use built-in and rebuild' button. Do not fall back silently to mixed vectors. Leave inbox files in place on model errors. Fix the doc: the installed app cannot run bge-m3; use `rhz serve` from pip and point MCP at that rhz.

findings.title: The MCP server resolves client, port and token once at startup: after any app relaunch every Claude tool fails until Claude Desktop restarts, and if it started before the app it stays an in-process writer for the whole session
findings.evidence: client() caches connect()'s result for the life of the process, and warm_up calls it before mcp.run(). HttpClient fixes base_url and the bearer token at construction, with no retry. The shell picks a fresh free_port and token on every launch and rewrites the token file. A live repro shows the cached client raising ConnectError while a fresh connect() succeeds. Tool failures are logged nowhere Rhizome owns, and the pip `rhizome-mcp` entry skips setup_logging.
findings.scenario: The user closes and reopens Rhizome at lunch. Every rhz_* call then returns '[WinError 10061]' for the rest of the day, with nothing telling the user to restart Claude. Or Claude starts at login before Rhizome, and MCP writes in-process all day with its own model load and vector cache.
findings.fix: Replace the singleton with a resolver keyed on the content of (server.json url, token). Re-resolve when it changes, or when a LocalClient is cached and the server comes up. Wrap tool bodies in _call: on httpx.ConnectError or 401, drop the client, re-run connect() and retry once; never retry on timeouts or 5xx, because ingest and decide are not idempotent. Return a readable bilingual error and log the mode on each reconnect. Keep warm_up's native imports. Point rhizome-mcp at the same bootstrap as `rhz mcp`. Add a test that swaps server and token between two calls.

findings.title: NCBI taxonomy lookups run inside materialize, under the write lock, during both ingest and rebuild, so rebuild is not deterministic or offline-replayable
findings.evidence: resolve_organism calls taxonomy_id for non-builtin names. rebuild wipes EntityAlias first, so every such organism hits the network again inside the rebuild transaction. A failure (offline, 429 parsed as a KeyError, timeout) falls through to organism:<name> instead of organism:taxon:N. Extraction.meta does not record taxa, contradicting the models.py invariant. With the local backend, judge and make_card also run under the lock.
findings.scenario: The user revokes a decision while offline or behind a flaky connection. The rebuild flips organism keys, merge decisions on organism:taxon keys quietly stop applying, and stalled connections hold the lock for 15 s per name.
findings.fix: Resolve taxa in ingest_text before any write, next to _check_ids, and store meta['taxa'] = {name: taxid|'not_found'|'unverified'}. resolve_organism then uses meta, then builtins, then the free key, and never touches the network. Before rebuild's deletes, snapshot the current organism alias→taxid resolution and backfill legacy extractions' meta from it. Retry 'unverified' only out-of-band. Run local-LLM judgements as queued jobs that commit per item.

findings.title: Ingest makes unbounded sequential external calls (up to 15 s each, no pooling or budget), so it can outlive the 60 s client timeout, and a retry gets a bare 'duplicate' answer
findings.evidence: Each OpenAlex, accession, repo and taxonomy check opens a new httpx.Client(timeout=15) and runs one after another. HttpClient uses a flat 60 s and rhz_ingest catches nothing. The server commits after the client has given up, and the sha-duplicate path returns only ok/duplicate/work_key with no suspect ids or related papers.
findings.scenario: From mainland China api.github.com stalls. A paper with 3 repos and 2 GEO ids takes ~90 s. Claude sees a ReadTimeout, edits a field and resubmits, and the paper ends up stored twice (or the retry loses the hallucination warnings).
findings.fix: Use one shared client with Timeout(8, connect=4) and a per-host circuit breaker: after one timeout, mark the remaining checks on that host 'unverified'. Optionally add a total deadline of ~20 s. Make the duplicate path return the stored suspect ids, repairs and related papers. Give HttpClient.ingest a ~180 s timeout. In rhz_ingest, catch timeouts and tell Claude to check rhz_search before resubmitting.

findings.title: Stale-job recovery requeues every running job at Worker start, including one actively running in another process
findings.evidence: recover_stale_jobs has no age or owner check, even though STALE_RUNNING exists. `rhz nightly` and LocalClient.create_topic run jobs through run_all in other processes, and the final status write is unconditional.
findings.scenario: `rhz nightly` starts a queued rebuild, and the user opens Rhizome two minutes later. The app reruns it concurrently, which produces lock failures, double backups, and job rows whose status is overwritten.
findings.fix: Add an owner_pid column, set it in the claim CAS, and requeue only rows whose pid is dead (system.pid_alive) or whose started_at is older than STALE_RUNNING. Write results only when status is running and the pid matches. Wrap the 'failed' write in try/except. Have CLI and LocalClient run only the job they enqueued.

findings.title: Inbox reads and moves the companion PDF without checking that it has finished arriving; truncated PDFs get stored in L0, and the post-commit move can orphan the PDF on Windows
findings.evidence: _stable() checks only the YAML, and the PDF is read immediately. file_done's PDF move happens after commit with no guard. SKIP_SUFFIXES excludes .pdf, so an orphaned or late PDF is never picked up. Explorer often preallocates the full size, which defeats size polling.
findings.scenario: The user drags paper.yaml and a 40 MB paper.pdf from USB. A partly written PDF is hashed into raw/, has_pdf is set and the tier is raised. Or the PDF stays in the inbox for good with no warning.
findings.fix: Check readiness by renaming or locking: move the YAML and PDF into inbox/.processing/<name>/ with retries and backoff, so a locked PDF means 'not ready'. Guard the PDF move and record a warning on failure. When a PDF arrives late for a YAML already in done/, attach it. List stray PDFs in inbox status.

findings.title: The inbox watcher starts the Observer only after the startup scan and has no liveness check or periodic rescan, so files can sit unprocessed until restart
findings.evidence: watch() runs scan() and only then schedules the Observer. Events during a long backlog are missed. A dead ReadDirectoryChangesW emitter after sleep or resume (OneDrive or network inbox) is never detected. scan() runs without the handler lock. Non-RXF files are only logged at INFO.
findings.scenario: After a laptop resume, every RXF saved from chat sits in the inbox. Home shows no failures, and the user concludes 'Rhizome 不收文件了'.
findings.fix: Start the Observer first, and run the scan and periodic rescans (every 30-60 s) under a shared module-level lock. Check obs and emitter is_alive and rebuild them with backoff. Expose {watching, last_scan, pending, ignored} in /stats and show 'N files waiting / not recognised' on Home.

findings.title: Anyone holding the API token can run local commands: PATCH /settings accepts hostile ssh_options and remotes, and the sync job runs them
findings.evidence: ssh_base appends ssh_options verbatim (`-oProxyCommand`), host is not validated, and remotes is patchable through the token-gated API. The token lives in the user's own files and the server binds to 127.0.0.1, so this mainly widens the blast radius of any future token leak.
findings.scenario: A leaked token, for example via a future XSS, lets an attacker send two requests and get a shell command run as the user within ~2 s.
findings.fix: Validate RemoteTarget fields (no leading '-', whitespace or control characters), and put '--' before host. Reject changes to ssh_options and control_path through PATCH so they are file/CLI-only. Set a real CSP in tauri.conf.json and on '/'.

findings.title: `rhz diag` ('settings without secrets') and GET /settings include database_url with the Postgres password
findings.evidence: diag dumps every Settings field except contact_email and remotes. Verified: a password in database_url appears verbatim in info.json.
findings.scenario: A user on the optional Postgres backend attaches the diag zip to a GitHub issue.
findings.fix: Redact with make_url(url).render_as_string(hide_password=True), falling back to '<redacted>' on parse failure. Fix the docstring to say the bundle contains local paths.

findings.title: The desktop shell writes the access token into backend-console.log, and the startup error pane can show it
findings.evidence: serve prints `{url}/#token=...` unconditionally, stdout is captured to the console log, and the error pane tails that log. The token rotates per desktop launch and is also stored in data_dir/token.
findings.scenario: A screenshot of a later-stage startup failure shared in a WeChat group or issue includes the token URL.
findings.fix: When RHIZOME_API_TOKEN is set (desktop mode), print only the URL without the token. Keep the full URL for interactive `rhz serve`.

findings.title: The token file and library get no Windows ACL, so moving the data dir to D:\ exposes them to other local accounts
findings.evidence: os.chmod(0o600) does nothing useful on Windows, and nothing sets a DACL. A moved target inherits Users:RX from the drive root.
findings.scenario: On a shared lab workstation, another account reads the token, the PDFs and the whole graph.
findings.fix: Add a secure_dir(path) helper: icacls by SID (current user plus *S-1-5-18), applied to the data-dir root on create and to the move target before copying. Warn when the target is outside the profile, and never apply it to existing non-empty or root folders.

findings.title: The backend is always TerminateProcess'd, so server.json goes stale; connect() then trusts any HTTP 200 on /health (at the stale URL or :8765) and crashes on a non-JSON answer
findings.evidence: child.kill() skips clear_server_marker. running_server_url never checks pid_alive. The probe accepts any 200 whose read_only is falsy and sends the bearer token. Only httpx.HTTPError is caught, so an HTML 200 raises JSONDecodeError and a list body raises AttributeError.
findings.scenario: A Vite or Jupyter server later binds 8765 or the old port. The MCP server or CLI either crashes at warm_up or sends the token to a foreign server and reports 401/404.
findings.fix: Have running_server_url return None when the marker's pid is dead. Add 'app': 'rhizome' to /health and require it. Catch (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError). Probe 8765 only when it is explicitly configured or no marker exists. Add a test with a fake {'ok': true} server.

findings.title: The `rhz serve` token never rotates, and the browser token capture pushes a history entry
findings.evidence: get_or_create_token reuses the token file across serve runs, and captureToken assigns location.hash, which adds a Back entry.
findings.scenario: Months later, Edge history or sync autocompletes a URL that still carries a live token on a shared profile.
findings.fix: Use history.replaceState in api.ts:17. Generate a fresh token on each `rhz serve` start and write it to the token file.

findings.title: No Host validation, and the unauthenticated /health reveals the version and language, so DNS rebinding can fingerprint the app
findings.evidence: /health returns {ok, version, read_only, language} for any Host header. All data endpoints are token-gated.
findings.scenario: A malicious page rebinds to 127.0.0.1 and confirms that Rhizome <version> is running and on which port.
findings.fix: When bound to loopback, reject Host values outside {127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]} with a custom check. Trim /health to {ok} and move version and language to an authenticated endpoint.

findings.title: MCP write tools have no annotations, so confirmation before rhz_decide relies on prose alone
findings.evidence: Every tool uses a bare @mcp.tool(). The effects are bounded (only queued items and actions) and revocable.
findings.scenario: A user who chose 'always allow' meets an injected sentence in a paper that pushes the model to merge without asking.
findings.fix: Add ToolAnnotations: readOnlyHint for the read tools, and destructiveHint=True for rhz_decide. Return the item kind, the sides and decision_id, and mention undo.

findings.title: A non-ASCII bearer value makes the auth dependency return 500 instead of 401
findings.evidence: secrets.compare_digest(str, str) raises TypeError on non-ASCII input.
findings.scenario: A scanner or a pasted CJK header fills rhizome.log with tracebacks.
findings.fix: Compare `.encode()` bytes, and check isascii() first.

findings.title: Hugging Face model loads are not pinned to a revision, so cached and fresh vectors can come from different weights under one model name
findings.evidence: MODEL_IDS are bare repo ids with no revision= argument. The embedder's name is the key, which is also the vector_cache key. This only applies to pip installs with [models].
findings.scenario: A new laptop downloads updated upstream weights, and the next rebuild mixes old cached vectors with new ones. Or a compromised repo ships a pickle.
findings.fix: Map each MODEL_ID to (repo, sha) and pass revision everywhere. Name the embedder 'bge-m3@sha7' so caches separate. Use allow_patterns to avoid .bin pickles, and raise the torch/transformers floors.

findings.title: release.yml publishes a public release from any claude/** branch push, with no tag/version check, no checksums, no concurrency guard and a branch-specific notes link
findings.evidence: `gh release create` runs whenever the tauri.conf.json version has no release yet. It is gated only by the smoke/e2e tests, not pytest or ruff, and a tag push never compares the tag with $ver. 'already exists; exit 0' silently keeps a broken asset. Installers are unsigned and have no SHA256SUMS.
findings.scenario: A WIP branch commit bumps the version and an untested installer is published. Or a broken 0.1.3 can't be replaced and stays the download.
findings.fix: Publish only on a v* tag or a workflow_dispatch input, and fail when the tag differs from v$ver. Run pytest and ruff inside the release job before publish. Write SHA256SUMS.txt (optionally with attest-build-provenance). Fail when an existing release's commit differs. Use tag-relative links in the release notes.

findings.title: App, MCP and CLI share one RotatingFileHandler: on Windows rollover fails and records are dropped, backups are destroyed, and stderr fills with tracebacks
findings.evidence: Every long-lived process (serve, mcp) opens logs/rhizome.log. os.rename fails while another process holds the file. Each failed doRollover still shifts and deletes the .N backups before the base rename fails. httpx and mcp INFO lines make the 2 MB limit reachable.
findings.scenario: About day 20 with Claude Desktop open, the logs stop being written and `rhz diag` ships a log that ends weeks ago.
findings.fix: Use per-role files (rhizome-serve.log, rhizome-mcp.log, rhizome-cli.log, delay=True). Make the rollover subclass catch OSError and back off. Set httpx, httpcore, mcp and similar loggers to WARNING. Update the diag glob to rhizome*.log*.

findings.title: Unhandled request exceptions (500s) never reach rhizome.log, and the log has no startup or shutdown markers and no level control in the frozen app
findings.evidence: uvicorn's default config sets propagate=False, so the 'Exception in ASGI application' traceback goes only to stderr. There is no app exception handler. serve logs nothing, watch_parent calls os._exit silently, and the level is hardcoded to INFO.
findings.scenario: A /search returns 500 and the user restarts; rhizome.log holds nothing about it.
findings.fix: Register @app.exception_handler(Exception) that calls log.exception with a request id and returns {detail, request_id}. Log version, data_dir, DB size and revision at serve start, a shutdown line, and a 'parent gone' line flushed before _exit. Read the level from RHIZOME_LOG_LEVEL.

findings.title: backend-console.log is in a different folder than documented, is truncated on every launch, and is missing from `rhz diag`
findings.evidence: The README and CI say %APPDATA%, but the shell uses app_log_dir (%LOCALAPPDATA%\dev.rhizome.desktop\logs). File::create truncates the file, and diag collects only rhizome.log*. The startup error page shows the correct path once.
findings.scenario: After a crash and a relaunch the traceback is gone, the diag bundle lacks it, and the support instructions point to a folder that doesn't exist.
findings.fix: Rotate the old file to backend-console.prev.log before File::create. Fix the README and CI path. Pass RHIZOME_CONSOLE_LOG to the child and include that file in diag.

findings.title: faulthandler is enabled only under RHIZOME_HANG_DUMP, so native crashes leave no trace
findings.evidence: There is no unconditional faulthandler.enable(), and the console log is truncated on relaunch.
findings.scenario: An access violation in numpy or the sqlite FTS code kills rhz.exe and leaves no stack trace.
findings.fix: Call faulthandler.enable(all_threads=True) in the CLI callback and in mcp main when stderr exists. Rotate the console log (see O3).

findings.title: The UI language choice is lost on every desktop launch, because localStorage is keyed to a random-port origin and the backend language is never read
findings.evidence: initialLanguage reads localStorage or navigator.language. Every launch is a new origin. The choice is PATCHed to the backend, but /health.language and /settings.ui_language are never read (api.health is unused). CLI and file changes never reach the UI.
findings.scenario: A user on Chinese Windows who prefers the English UI has to switch it back on every launch, and backend messages come out in a different language from the UI.
findings.fix: At boot in main.tsx, call api.health() (with a ~1.5 s timeout) and map language to 'zh-CN' or 'en' before rendering. Keep localStorage only as a first-paint cache. Never use a fixed port.

findings.title: A spawn-failure message can be lost (eval runs before the loading page exists), and setup errors panic silently in a windowless process
findings.evidence: show_error evals into the window before navigation to the loading page completes. The watcher thread never starts on that path. Using `?` on resource_dir, log_dir or free_port makes setup panic with no window. The loading page has no timeout.
findings.scenario: 360 quarantines the unsigned rhz.exe, the spawn fails, and the window shows '正在启动…' forever.
findings.fix: Store startup errors in managed state and show them from on_page_load(Finished). Never return Err from setup. Add a ~120 s timeout to the loading page that points at the log dir. Write fatal errors to shell.log, and mention antivirus quarantine in the message.

findings.title: The parent watchdog relies on a reusable PID, so a recycled PID leaves an orphan rhz.exe holding the DB and running a second watcher and worker
findings.evidence: pid_alive re-opens the PID by number every 2 s, and there is no Job Object.
findings.scenario: After a shell crash, Windows hands that PID to another process and rhz.exe never exits.
findings.fix: On Windows, OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE) once at start and WaitForSingleObject on the handle; holding the handle prevents PID reuse. Optionally add a Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE.

findings.title: The upgrade installer hard-kills every rhz.exe, including Claude's MCP child, before asking, so Cancel leaves a dead window; downgrades are not blocked
findings.evidence: NSIS_HOOK_PREINSTALL runs taskkill /F /IM rhz.exe before Tauri's CheckIfAppIsRunning prompt, and allowDowngrades defaults to true.
findings.scenario: The user clicks Cancel at 'Rhizome is running'. The backend is already dead behind the open window, and Claude's tools are disconnected with no message.
findings.fix: In the hook, FindProcess Rhizome.exe and show a bilingual OK/Cancel before killing anything (Abort on Cancel), then kill Rhizome.exe and rhz.exe. Add 'restart Claude Desktop after upgrading' to the finish text. Guard downgrades in the backend (U2).

findings.title: The default 1320×880 window with a 900×600 minimum overflows 1366×768 laptops at 125-150% scaling, and window state is not persisted
findings.evidence: There is no monitor clamping and no window-state plugin.
findings.scenario: On a common university laptop the window is larger than the screen.
findings.fix: Set preventOverflow: true, lower the minimum to ~800×480, and optionally add tauri-plugin-window-state (size, position, maximized only).

findings.title: There is no update notification, so a user never learns that a fixed version exists
findings.evidence: The updater and signing are deferred, and nothing queries the releases feed.
findings.scenario: A data-loss fix in 0.1.3 goes unnoticed for a year.
findings.fix: Have the worker check GitHub releases/latest once a day (respecting offline), store the result in KV, and show a dismissible banner. Switch to tauri-plugin-updater once signing exists.

findings.title: Mouse back or Alt+Left lands on the dead 'Starting Rhizome…' loading page, because both the shell navigate and the token capture push history entries
findings.evidence: History ends up as [loading page, #token=…, #/, ...routes]. The loading page is static and spins forever once the poll thread has returned.
findings.scenario: A Windows mouse user presses the thumb-back button past Home, decides the app has hung, and kills it.
findings.fix: In main.rs, eval location.replace('<url>') (falling back to navigate). In api.ts, use history.replaceState(null,'','#/') before the router mounts. Keep accelerator keys enabled.

findings.title: The recall and search keyword step builds an FTS5 OR of every word with no dedup or cap, taking 10-66 s for long contexts on large libraries
findings.evidence: _fts_query ORs every normalised term of 3+ characters, including duplicates and stopwords. recall passes context[:4000]. Measured with duplicates kept: 230 terms take 11.6 s and 600 terms 69.5 s; deduplicated, the same sets take 1.0 s and 2.9 s.
findings.scenario: Claude calls rhz_recall on a pasted draft paragraph. With a few thousand papers it passes the 60 s timeout and the headline MCP feature fails.
findings.fix: Deduplicate terms in order, drop stopwords, and keep at most ~12 (longest first). Have recall send a reduced query, or skip FTS for long contexts and rely on knn plus the rerank. Add a test that a 4,000-character context produces ≤12 phrases.

findings.title: entity_card loads every edge of hub nodes (11k edges, 3.4 MB); the UI renders them all, rhz_get returns them to Claude, and the review queue rebuilds the card for every item
findings.evidence: There is no LIMIT, despite the module docstring's '~300 element cap'. review._context builds a full card per side and keeps only 3 connections. rhz_get strips only exports.raw.
findings.scenario: 'rhz_get organism:taxon:9606' overruns Claude's context, and clicking Homo sapiens freezes the UI.
findings.fix: Return per-type counts plus the top N (~50) edges per type, with a paged /entity/{id}/edges endpoint. Give _context its own cheap queries. Make rhz_get return the summary form by default.

findings.title: neighbors(hops=2) loads the full two-hop neighbourhood into memory before paging (12 s, 233 MB) and exceeds the Windows SQLite bind-variable limit for large hubs
findings.evidence: Each hop binds the whole frontier twice and loads every Edge object, and only then slices to 150 nodes. Hubs with more than 16,383 neighbours hit Windows SQLite's 32,766 limit. Edges are cut by id.
findings.scenario: Choosing '2 跳' on an organism or a large topic stalls a thread for 10+ s, or returns 500 on Windows.
findings.fix: Express both hops as subqueries, skip expanding hub nodes, page in SQL with ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET plus a count, and fetch edges only among the page nodes. Show 'showing 150 of N' in the UI.

findings.title: topic_assets has no element cap: the root topic gives 45k items (13.8 MB) and fails with 'too many SQL variables' on Windows, and the Topic page renders it all and refetches on every role click
findings.evidence: Python sets are passed back through expanding IN lists (all_ids), and there is no cap. topic_changes behaves the same way. Each role chip refetches, and the Loading indicator is hidden once data exists.
findings.scenario: Opening the broadest topic in a 5k-paper library returns 500 on Windows, or freezes the webview.
findings.fix: Aggregate in SQL with per-column LIMIT plus counts and an offset per column, never binding id lists. On the frontend, fetch once, filter roles with useMemo, show 150 per column with 'Show more', and dim the view while reloading.

findings.title: Every ingest does work proportional to the whole library: link_citations parses all OpenAlex JSON, and promote_topics runs one COUNT per candidate
findings.evidence: Even with only_work_ids, every current openalex Extraction is loaded and filtered in Python. This adds about 2 s per ingest at 10k papers, inside the write transaction.
findings.scenario: Batch ingest latency keeps growing as the library grows.
findings.fix: For outgoing links, look up only this work's references. For incoming links, use a json_each SQL query. Run promote_topics only over this work's topics and use one GROUP BY.

findings.title: Vector cache: +465 MB RSS and a 2.4 s cold load per process, a 2× peak from .all()+stack, concurrent loads, rebuild thrash, and nothing warms it
findings.evidence: Loading materialises all BLOBs and then stacks them, and the lock guards only the dict. The worker's uncommitted rebuild view and readers' committed view evict each other on signature mismatch. The first knn after start pays the load. connect imports FastAPI only to find the token path.
findings.scenario: The first search after waking the laptop takes seconds, and memory spikes during a rebuild while searching.
findings.fix: Preallocate from the count and stream with yield_per. Make loads single-flight. Give rebuild a private cache instance. Preload in a lifespan daemon thread when the app is writable, and in MCP only for LocalClient. Move token_path into config. Optionally store vectors as float16.

findings.title: entity_fts.entity_id is UNINDEXED but Graph.reindex deletes by it, causing a full scan on every reindex
findings.evidence: Measured: 27.6 ms per delete at 55k rows, against 0.1 ms by rowid, with 12-25 reindexes per ingest.
findings.scenario: Ingest and rebuild slow down linearly as the library grows.
findings.fix: Use rowid = entity id for inserts and deletes. Ship migration 0002 to recreate entity_fts (it can be combined with the D8 rederive).

findings.title: Chinese keyword search is broken: multi-character CJK queries never match FTS, and the LIKE fallback matches single characters and pollutes RRF
findings.evidence: An unspaced CJK query becomes one exact phrase, which almost never matches. With fewer than 200 FTS hits the LIKE fallback runs on the first 6 single characters, returns up to 200 arbitrary rows, and RRF gives them full rank credit. The lexical reranker also scores single CJK characters. Trigram cannot match a 2-character query.
findings.scenario: The Chinese-speaking user searches '小鼠单细胞数据', and half of the first page is entities that merely contain 数 or 单.
findings.fix: For CJK runs of 3 or more characters, emit overlapping 3-character windows ORed together (capped at ~24). Use LIKE only for 2-character CJK runs and short Latin tokens, with bigrams and never single characters, rank those hits by bigram matches, and place them after the FTS hits. Use bigrams in LexicalReranker. Add tests.

findings.title: Synthesis runs one knn per recent asset with no cap inside the nightly transaction, looks at a fixed 7-day window, and stops at 20 pairs in arbitrary order
findings.evidence: Each asset reruns the signature query and a full matmul (11.7 s for 750 assets). The query has no ORDER BY and returns at 20 items, so the first assets by rowid fill every slot. Because synthesis runs at most weekly, assets between runs are never sources.
findings.scenario: After a bulk-import week the nightly holds the write lock for 20+ minutes, and most of that week's assets are skipped for good.
findings.fix: Call VECTORS.get once, batch the matmul in chunks, collect all pairs above the threshold, sort by similarity, cap with at most 1-2 pairs per source, and limit to the newest 2,000 sources. Set since = last_synthesis (or the watermark of what was scanned). Do the computation before writing, then insert in one short transaction.

findings.title: Without NLI, opposing claims (precede/follow, increase/decrease, Chinese 没有/并非) are silently auto-merged into one claim node
findings.evidence: With the default nli='none', resolve_claim diverts only candidates whose negation parity differs. _negated tokenises CJK one character at a time, so 没有 and 并非 never count, while 无监督 and 不同 count falsely. Antonyms are not considered. resolve_free auto-merges at ≥0.9 with only an alias row and no review item. Reproduced at 0.948 for a long 没有 pair.
findings.scenario: A rebuttal paper's claim is merged into the claim it argues against. Both papers 'support' one node and the contradiction list stays empty, with no way to split them.
findings.fix: In the path without NLI, never auto-merge claims; cap them at merge_review so they are queued. Add antonym pairs (EN/ZH) and a leftmost-longest Chinese negation regex with an exclusion list, routing such pairs to contradiction review. Add tests.

findings.title: With the default models, canonicalisation catches only lexical variants: synonyms, acronyms and ZH/EN pairs are never merged or queued
findings.evidence: scRNA-seq vs single-cell RNA sequencing scores 0.27, below merge_review. The vocab loop is the main defence, but it is cold early on.
findings.scenario: By day 30, 'GRN inference', 'gene regulatory network inference' and '基因调控网络推断' are three separate topics.
findings.fix: Let RXF topics carry aliases (en/zh) and update the export prompt. Add an acronym/initials check that queues the pair at merge_review. Show 'lexical matching only' in Settings while hashing is the embedder.

findings.title: One threshold set is applied to two incompatible score scales, several gates are hard-coded, and the tuned synthesis threshold survives a model switch
findings.evidence: The lexical and bge scales differ. The 0.35/0.2/0.3 literals are not in config. The KV synthesis_sim value has no model tag.
findings.scenario: After switching to bge-m3, recall and synthesis gates pass nearly everything, or a value learned under hashing floods or empties the digest.
findings.fix: Keep per-model threshold profiles, move the literals into Thresholds, key the learned values by embedder (see M11), and reset to the profile when the model changes.

findings.title: When rebuilding under a new model, a human merge is silently discarded if the new model auto-merges the source elsewhere first
findings.evidence: by_key(A) follows the redirect to B, which doesn't exist yet, and returns None. A then auto-merges into C. When the merge is replayed, _op_merge finds no src and returns True, counting the decision as applied.
findings.scenario: After switching to bge-reranker, 'A is B' quietly becomes A in C, and the decision list still shows it as active.
findings.fix: In resolve_free and resolve_claim, when the key is redirected and the target is missing, create the entity and skip knn and auto-merge. Make _op_merge's already-merged branch verify the result and queue a conflict otherwise. Add a regression test.

findings.title: Without a local judge, retro-tagging queues up to 500 review items per topic, has no bulk dismiss, and the items survive rebuilds
findings.evidence: QueueBackend is the default, and every kept candidate is queued with no cap.
findings.scenario: Ten topics in a week produce thousands of 'is this about X?' items.
findings.fix: Add retro_queue_max (~30) sorted by score; dedupe keys page through the rest when the job is rerun. Return a remaining count. Add POST /review/dismiss {kind, topic} and a UI button. Mark old items obsolete when a topic is redefined.

findings.title: Model management: full-repo snapshots (~9.5 GB into Roaming), no mirror hint, downloads triggered inside requests and ignoring offline, and an ONNX path that never engages
findings.evidence: snapshot_download has no allow_patterns. The ONNX backend needs optimum, which is not installed, and the fallback logs at INFO. local_files_only is never set, and offline only covers lookups. This only affects pip [models] installs, because the frozen build excludes them.
findings.scenario: A user in China gets a stalled download inside an ingest. Successful downloads put GBs of unused files under the roaming profile.
findings.fix: Use allow_patterns matching the backend that is actually loaded. Drop the ONNX attempt and onnxruntime, or make it an explicit opt-in. Set local_files_only=offline, and raise 'run rhz models download X' when files are missing. Wrap network errors with an HF_ENDPOINT/proxy hint. Fix the design doc.

findings.title: FSRS daily caps use UTC midnight, and new cards are ordered by hash id
findings.evidence: _day_start truncates utcnow(), which rolls over at 08:00 in Beijing. ReviewCard has no created_at column.
findings.scenario: At 07:30 the user sees no new cards. Last month's cards come before this week's.
findings.fix: Use a local day with a rollover hour (4), converted back to naive UTC. Add a nullable created_at and order new cards by priority then created_at desc.

findings.title: The retrieval gate is a smoke test: one synthetic question can never hit, and the 0.8 threshold hides it
findings.evidence: `expect: [claim]` never matches claim:<sha>. 5/6 passes. The test patches the fixture, but release runs the raw file.
findings.scenario: A regression that breaks claim retrieval still passes CI and the release gate.
findings.fix: Support type~alias expect entries that resolve once (and error when missing), use the same file for the test and the release, assert every question hits, and add distractor questions.

findings.title: NCBI esearch error payloads (HTTP 200 with ERROR and no count) are read as not_found, so real accessions are dropped permanently as hallucinations
findings.evidence: `.get('count', 0)` turns a backend error into not_found. The verdict is frozen in meta.checks and replayed by rebuild, a re-drop is a sha duplicate, and nothing ever re-checks. suspect_ids is a union, so it never clears.
findings.scenario: An NCBI hiccup marks a real GSE as 疑似幻觉, the dataset node is never created, and the user has to edit bytes to re-ingest.
findings.fix: Return unverified when ERROR is present, count is missing or errorlist is non-trivial; only an explicit 0 means not_found. Retry once and send tool/email. Return unverified for ENA/DDBJ ids that NCBI reports as 0. Add `rhz recheck` (and a UI button) that re-runs checks, recomputes suspect_ids from scratch and re-materialises.

findings.title: Chinese national repositories (GSA/NGDC: PRJCA, CRA, HRA, OMIX, SAMC) are rejected or reported NCBI-not_found, while CNGB and Zenodo are never checked
findings.evidence: With no database label, CRA and HRA fail the format check (bad_format) and the node is dropped. Any PRJ* id goes to NCBI bioproject, so PRJCA comes back not_found and is dropped. Zenodo DOI and bare ids produce two keys.
findings.scenario: A Chinese researcher's paper with GSA-Human data loses exactly the dataset they most need, and gets flagged as a hallucination.
findings.fix: Add a GSA pattern and database label, accept matches when the label is wrong, narrow the NCBI routing to PRJNA/PRJEB/PRJDB, and return unverified for databases that are not indexed. Optionally add a Zenodo record check and a normalised key. Add download hints and tests.

findings.title: 'bad_format' treats mislabelled-but-real accessions and non-canonical repo URLs as fabrication, so they are dropped and the paper is flagged
findings.evidence: GSE labelled SRA fails, as do github /tree/ and /blob/ links, ssh URLs, and gitee/zenodo/huggingface hosts. The URL is stripped from the method.
findings.scenario: Correct IDs show a 'suspected hallucinated' warning, which erodes trust in the one safety signal the product has.
findings.fix: Parse repos with urllib in normalize_repo (first two path segments, ssh form, gitee). Record well-formed URLs on other hosts as 'unanchored' and keep the URL. When the label is wrong but guess_database matches, verify against the guessed database and relabel. Add a recompute path, since meta.checks is frozen.

findings.title: OpenAlex enrichment happens once and fails silently: a transient 429/5xx or offline mode permanently loses the abstract, venue and citation edges
findings.evidence: A non-200 returns None without logging, and nothing ever fetches again. Duplicate re-drops short-circuit. The only callers are at ingest time.
findings.scenario: During an OpenAlex 503 window, 15 dropped exports end up with no abstract or cites and openalex_id NULL, and they can never be linked.
findings.fix: Have fetch_work return a status (ok/not_found/transient) with brief retries honouring Retry-After. Add a backfill job (`rhz enrich`, plus a nightly step when online) that selects works with DOIs and no current openalex extraction, and reuses an attach_openalex helper plus link_citations for the enriched ids. Show a 'missing T0' count.

findings.title: DOI normalisation misses common artefacts, and '#' or '?' in a DOI truncates the OpenAlex lookup URL
findings.evidence: Only strip and lower-casing are applied. A trailing '.', 'DOI: ' or dx.doi.org survives. The DOI is put raw into the URL path. doi_ok is unused.
findings.scenario: A sentence-final period from an LLM export gives an OpenAlex 404 and a duplicate work key later.
findings.fix: Centralise normalize_doi: strip prefixes and unbalanced trailing punctuation, lower-case. Use it in the schema and work_key, gate calls with doi_ok, and percent-encode or use filter=doi:. Add tests.

findings.title: GitHub verification is unauthenticated (60/h) and uncached, and a 'verified' status is written once and never upgraded
findings.evidence: After a 403, remaining repos are 'unverified' forever. Popular repos are re-verified on every ingest.
findings.scenario: A batch ingest exhausts the limit and the 已核实 badges are missing permanently.
findings.fix: Upgrade verified on the existing-entity paths. Skip the network when the entity is already anchored and verified. Treat rate-limit 403 as exhausted until the reset time.

findings.title: Network failures are invisible: no connectivity diagnostics, no use of the Windows certificate store, no proxy guidance, and contact_email cannot be set from the UI
findings.evidence: httpx uses only certifi, and every failure collapses to 'unverified' or None, recorded only at ingest.
findings.scenario: Behind a TLS-inspecting proxy, no paper ever gets an abstract or a verified badge, and the UI gives no hint why.
findings.fix: Use a truststore SSLContext (bundled), keep per-host failure counters exposed in the status API with a Settings banner, add `rhz doctor` probes into diag, add a contact_email input, and add a README note on HTTPS_PROXY. Pair with the N6 backfill.

findings.title: NCBI E-utilities etiquette is not followed: no tool/email/api_key and no 3 req/s throttle
findings.evidence: The User-Agent mailto does not count as the tool/email parameters, and there is no pacing.
findings.scenario: Concurrent ingests trigger 429s, and datasets are stored as 'unverified'.
findings.fix: Add tool, email and optional api_key parameters, a module lock with 0.34 s spacing, per-run caching, and one retry honouring Retry-After.

findings.title: fetch_work catches only HTTPError and ValueError, so an unexpected OpenAlex payload aborts the whole ingest and sends the file to error/
findings.evidence: `w['id']` and `a['author']['display_name']` sit outside the try block.
findings.scenario: An OpenAlex schema change means every DOI ingest lands in error/.
findings.fix: Parse with .get() chains, catch any Exception, log it with the DOI and return None. Add a test with a malformed payload.

findings.title: No tests exercise verify.py or openalex.py response handling
findings.evidence: check_accession is monkeypatched wholesale and offline is forced. Coverage is 34-43%.
findings.scenario: Fixes to N3, N5 or N11, or an httpx upgrade, regress silently.
findings.fix: Add test_external.py with offline turned off and httpx.MockTransport patched into each module's imported client. Use table-driven cases for esearch, BioStudies, GitHub, taxonomy and fetch_work, plus one ingest test over a 5xx.

findings.title: Background jobs are write-only: no job list, no UI polling, no dedupe, a fixed 1.5 s reload, and a failing nightly silently reruns every 30 minutes
findings.evidence: The frontend never calls GET /jobs/{id}. last_nightly is written only on success, so failures re-enqueue on the 900-tick cycle. format_exc(limit=5) keeps only the outer frames. Clicking 重算 repeatedly queues sequential full rebuilds.
findings.scenario: Weekly synthesis and promotion stop for a month after an upgrade with no sign in the UI. Five clicks on 重算 produce five rebuilds and five backups.
findings.fix: Coalesce queued idempotent kinds (rebuild, nightly). Back off after consecutive nightly failures. Keep the inner traceback frames. Add GET /jobs?kind&active plus last failure in /stats. Add a useJob hook that polls, disables buttons and shows errors, and reloads the Digest when the job is done.

findings.title: There is no React error boundary or global error handler, so any render or effect exception (e.g. WebGL/Sigma) blanks the whole window
findings.evidence: React 18 unmounts the root. `new Sigma` has no guard. There are no error or unhandledrejection listeners.
findings.scenario: Without WebGL, opening 主题地图 turns the whole app white until restart.
findings.fix: Add a top-level ErrorBoundary inside the layout, reset on route change, that shows the error, a copy-details button and a 'Go home' link. Wrap the Sigma constructor in try/catch with a list fallback. Add a global listener that shows a toast.

findings.title: UI mutations fail silently and <Loading> discards the server's error detail: about 15 calls with no catch, no read-only awareness
findings.evidence: Rejections are unhandled. Loading maps only 401 and 404, so everything else is 出错了. /health.read_only is never read, so on a read-only snapshot every write button silently gets 403.
findings.scenario: The DB is locked or the sidecar is gone, and confirm, merge or grade do nothing with no message. The user thinks a correction was saved.
findings.fix: Add an errorText(e) helper (FastAPI 422 list, detail.report, network TypeError mapped to 'cannot reach'). Add a toast store and a run() wrapper used by every mutation, and show status+detail with a copy button in Loading. Read read_only at boot to disable write controls and show a banner.

findings.title: `rhz diag` needs a healthy, migratable DB (it runs init_db), leaves out most of what a bug report needs, and can't be reached from the app
findings.evidence: diag calls init_db (which migrates) and home_stats with no try. It collects only rhizome.log*, with no revision, quick_check, failed jobs or inbox error reports. platform is just 'win32'.
findings.scenario: A failed 0.2 migration means `rhz diag` crashes with the same error and produces no zip.
findings.fix: Open the DB read-only and wrap each section, writing errors.txt. Include revisions, quick_check, size, failed jobs, the console log, error reports, platform.platform() and frozen. Rotate the console log. Point the startup error page at `rhz.cmd diag`.

findings.title: CLI errors surface as false success or raw tracebacks: `rhz decide` prints 'ok' and exits 0 on a 422, and domain errors and bad snapshot paths dump stack traces
findings.evidence: _post turns a 422 into {ok: false}, and decide ignores it. A 404 raises HTTPStatusError and local mode raises ValueError, both shown as tracebacks. A quoted '~' snapshot path gives a 145-line traceback, and read-only PermissionError is raw too.
findings.scenario: `rhz decide 12 merge` on the wrong kind prints 'ok' and the item stays pending. On HPC a quoted tilde breaks every command with an opaque trace.
findings.fix: Add a _check(r) helper that prints in red and raises typer.Exit(1) on ok=False, used by decide, topic and the other _post users. Map 404 to {ok: false} too. Have LocalClient catch expected domain errors and return the same shape. Add a run() entry wrapper that turns RhizomeError or PermissionError into a one-liner (JSON in --json mode). expanduser the snapshot path and validate it with BadParameter.

findings.title: ci.yml has never run: unit tests, ruff, license, i18n, SPDX and gitleaks checks ran zero times while three releases were published
findings.evidence: ci.yml triggers only on push to main or PRs. No main branch exists, there are no PRs, and every run is release.yml. The Windows pytest cell has never run. gitleaks lacks fetch-depth 0, and no job has a timeout.
findings.scenario: A Windows-only regression in ingest or decisions ships, because release smoke tests don't touch those areas.
findings.fix: Run pytest and ruff inside release.yml before publish (or call ci.yml via workflow_call with needs). Add claude/** and workflow_dispatch to the ci.yml triggers. Set fetch-depth 0 for gitleaks and timeout-minutes on each job.

findings.title: The background worker, the nightly scheduler and the inbox watcher threads are never run by any test
findings.evidence: The helpers are unit-tested, but the loop glue is not. The nightly trigger counts idle ticks.
findings.scenario: A loop regression silently stops nightly runs, and no test fails.
findings.fix: Extract Worker.step() with a wall-clock nightly check and test it synchronously. Add one TestClient lifespan smoke test with a short interval. Test _Handler._handle directly with a CJK path.

findings.title: The upgrade path is untested: no install-over-previous e2e, no multi-revision migration test, and the backup-then-migrate branch has no coverage
findings.evidence: Only 0001 exists, and the e2e does only a clean install.
findings.scenario: The first real migration ever executed runs on the user's only library.
findings.fix: Add test_migrations.py parametrised over revisions (upgrade from each base, row and FTS checks, backup check), using a dummy 0002 now. Commit a fixture DB from an old version and load it in e2e. Add the full install-over-previous run when a schema change ships.

findings.title: HttpClient (used whenever the app runs) has no test coverage, and its error behaviour differs from LocalClient's, so MCP tools act differently depending on whether the app is open
findings.evidence: Over HTTP an invalid action returns JSON {ok: false}; locally it raises ValueError. recall and create_topic index ['results'] on an error dict. limit=500 returns 422 only over HTTP. Glue such as related and create_topic is duplicated.
findings.scenario: Claude's retry logic sees an error JSON one day and an isError result the next. Queue paging fails only when the app is open.
findings.fix: Add an MCP _call wrapper that normalises every exception to {ok: false, error}. Clamp limits to shared constants. Map 404 and 422 consistently. Parametrise tests over LocalClient and HttpClient(TestClient) with negative cases.

findings.title: The MCP server is tested only as plain functions; the JSON-RPC layer is covered by one rhz_search smoke test
findings.evidence: rhz_related and rhz_decide are never called, and the test reads the private _tool_manager.
findings.scenario: A constraints bump that changes FastMCP schemas passes CI.
findings.fix: Use create_connected_server_and_client_session to list and call all tools, including error cases. Extend the smoke test.

findings.title: CI tests against floating dependencies and a floating toolchain while the installer ships constraints.txt pins; PyInstaller is unpinned
findings.evidence: The unit suite never runs against the shipped set. Rust stable, windows-latest and ruff all float.
findings.scenario: An upstream release turns CI red, or a pin-specific bug ships.
