findings.fix: Add a Windows cell installing with -c constraints.txt. Pin pyinstaller, its hooks and setuptools in the constraints, add rust-toolchain.toml, and pin ruff.

findings.title: There is no type checking in CI; mypy reports 34+ errors, a few of them real Optional dereferences
findings.evidence: Most errors are false positives. upsert_edge returning None is dereferenced in _op_edge_status.
findings.scenario: A rare None crashes a decision.
findings.fix: Raise DecisionError on None at decisions.py:168. Add need_key/need_id helpers. Add a non-blocking mypy step on pipeline/ and services/.

findings.title: 15 of 27 CLI commands are never invoked by a test
findings.evidence: settings set (type coercion), backup, models download and others have no test. A bad key in settings set raises a raw KeyError.
findings.scenario: A typo-level regression in `rhz settings set` corrupts settings.json.
findings.fix: Parametrise a --help test over all commands. Add focused tests for settings set and backup. Validate keys against model_fields.

findings.title: The frontend has no tests, lint or API-contract check, and the Tauri shell has no unit tests
findings.evidence: tsc runs in CI, but backend field renames are not checked against the TS interfaces.
findings.scenario: A renamed field renders empty cards.
findings.fix: Add a pytest contract test asserting that key routes return the fields api.ts reads. Add a serde_json_string unit test, or use serde_json.

findings.title: There is no scale or two-process test fixture; everything runs on three papers in one process
findings.evidence: Deferred transactions with WAL can return SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT straight away. The only lock test fakes the error.
findings.scenario: An MCP LocalClient and the app worker ingesting at the same time fail, and no test catches it.
findings.fix: Add a multiprocessing test where two LocalClients ingest in a loop and assert no OperationalError. Use BEGIN IMMEDIATE for write sessions where it fits. Add an opt-in bench marker that records timings at ~2k works.

findings.title: check_licenses.py flags dual-licence npm lists as copyleft, crashes on empty input, and scans the runner environment rather than the shipped pins
findings.evidence: `' '.join(list)` treats a dual licence as one string. json.load has no guard. The scan runs over the dev environment.
findings.scenario: A misleading CI failure, or a GPL dependency that ships unnoticed.
findings.fix: Treat list licences as options, error clearly on empty stdin, and run pip-licenses in release.yml over the constrained environment (ignoring PyInstaller explicitly).

findings.title: The offline installer variant is published but never installed or checked in CI
findings.evidence: The copy reuses $std.FullName, and e2e picks only *_x64-setup.exe.
findings.scenario: The air-gapped installer is the one that's broken.
findings.fix: Resolve the file freshly after the offline build, and assert its size is >100 MB more than the standard one and its hash differs.

findings.title: Env vars override explicit Settings arguments, so pytest (and `rhz --data-dir`/`--snapshot`) follow RHIZOME_* from the shell into the user's real library
findings.evidence: settings_customise_sources returns (env, init). Reproduced: with RHIZOME_DATA_DIR set, pytest wrote rhizome.db and backups into the 'real' dir and overwrote settings.json with offline=true and zh_CN. A full run would `rebuild --no-backup` there. The same precedence lets a stray RHIZOME_DATABASE_URL redirect a snapshot.
findings.scenario: The maintainer, who is also the only user, runs pytest with RHIZOME_DATA_DIR in their profile, and their library is rebuilt and its settings changed.
findings.fix: Add an autouse fixture that deletes every RHIZOME_* var and sets OFFLINE, and assert the data_dir in the settings fixture. In config.py, order sources as init > env > file, with a dedicated settings.json source; or apply snapshot and --data-dir with model_copy after construction. Add regression tests.

findings.title: L1 replay validates every stored RXF row against the current model, not its stored version, and rebuild silently drops rows that fail
findings.evidence: A strict model (extra=forbid) is applied, ex.schema_version is ignored, exceptions are logged and skipped, and the summary has counts only with exit 0.
findings.scenario: A future RXF change, or an optional field removed by accident, makes 188 papers vanish from L2 after a rebuild with no report.
findings.fix: Pre-flight validate every row before the deletes and abort with a list unless forced. Collect failures into the summary and exit 1. Dispatch on the stored version via SCHEMAS plus an upcast. Add golden-fixture tests per version.

findings.title: Durable entity keys depend on text.norm(), so any change to normalisation orphans decisions, cards and access history and breaks rebuild
findings.evidence: No norm_version or remap tool exists. Decisions on keys that changed raise DecisionError and abort the rebuild (D1). entity_alias.norm goes stale and causes duplicates.
findings.scenario: 0.2 adds 《》“” to _PUNCT, and the user's rebuild fails or cards lose their entities.
findings.fix: Add a golden test pinning norm and free_key outputs, plus a code comment. When norm changes, ship a data migration that recomputes alias norms and rewrites keys in decisions, cards, access logs and retro outputs.

findings.title: settings.json is written non-atomically and any load error (bad JSON or one invalid enum) aborts the app, CLI and MCP before logging starts
findings.evidence: json.loads plus Settings(**) run with no handling, and write_text truncates in place. Verified: 'embedder': 'bge-m3-v2' raises ValidationError.
findings.scenario: A torn write, a Notepad edit ('zh-CN') or a downgrade means a traceback at every launch.
findings.fix: Use tmp+fsync+os.replace with a .bak. On parse failure, try .bak. On validation failure, drop only the failing fields, record settings_problems, and show them in the UI and as a CLI one-liner. Never silently fall back to full defaults when the file existed, and make the pointer write atomic too.

findings.title: Saving settings persists the whole effective model: defaults freeze at first save, unknown keys are dropped, and env, --port and --lang overrides are baked in
findings.evidence: model_dump writes all 17 fields, including every threshold, the sidecar's random port and env values. Verified: one language toggle wrote port=54321 and offline=true. extra='ignore' then deletes keys from newer versions. The thresholds are documented as uncalibrated and due to change.
findings.scenario: Day 1, a language toggle freezes every threshold, so the calibrated defaults in 0.2 never reach this user. A one-off RHIZOME_OFFLINE disables OpenAlex for good. `rhz serve` binds a stale random port.
findings.fix: Replace save_settings with update_settings(patch): read the raw JSON, deep-merge only the changed keys, drop values equal to class defaults, keep unknown keys, add settings_version, validate, and write atomically. Make PATCH and the CLI send deltas, with null meaning reset. Migrate v0.1 files once by removing keys equal to the 0.1 defaults.

findings.title: RXF version rough edges: a quoted rxf_version is rejected with a self-contradictory message, and prompt_version has no registry
findings.evidence: 'rxf_version: "1"' gives '1 unsupported; supported: 1'. The instructions say deep-review-v2 while the examples say v3.
findings.scenario: Claude quotes the version and the user gets a contradictory error.
findings.fix: Coerce digit strings and integral floats to int before the lookup and record a repair. Use repr in the message. Align the instructions' prompt_version and add a contract test.

findings.title: review_card.state is an unversioned py-fsrs dict, so a major py-fsrs change breaks grading every existing card
findings.evidence: Card.from_dict indexes fixed keys, and the bound allows fsrs>=5,<7.
findings.scenario: Raising the upper bound causes a KeyError on every review.
findings.fix: Pin fsrs>=6,<7, add a test grading a hard-coded 6.x dict, and on mismatch fall back to replaying ReviewLog.

findings.title: Search and browse are silently capped at 20 results with no paging, the count label is wrong, and filtered browse only looks at the 500 newest ids
findings.evidence: No limit or offset is sent, and n = results.length. browse applies .limit(500) before filters, so older matches never appear.
findings.scenario: With 5,000 papers, the Papers tile shows '20 results', and a filter for year ≤2015 returns nothing.
findings.fix: Push browse filters into SQL with LIMIT/OFFSET and an exact total. For text search, fetch limit+1 and return has_more. Keep offset in the hash, add 'load more', and show honest labels.

findings.title: The Search page filter form gets out of sync with the URL after a top-bar search, because the state is seeded once and the component is not keyed
findings.evidence: useState(() => query) runs once, and results follow the URL.
findings.scenario: The input shows 'ATAC' while the results are for 'scVI', and pressing Enter resubmits the stale query.
findings.fix: Use `<SearchPage key={route.query.toString()}>`, or sync with a useEffect on query.

findings.title: Hash navigation never resets scroll, and page filters are not stored in the URL
findings.evidence: There is no scrollTo, and kind, hops and role are local state.
findings.scenario: An entity page opens scrolled down, and Back loses the Review filter.
findings.fix: Call scrollTo(0,0) on hashchange, and move the filters into the hash query.

findings.title: Keyboard shortcuts have no repeat, in-flight or modifier guard, so a held or double key grades one card twice
findings.evidence: The only guard is the !shown check, applied after the await. Ctrl+S triggers skip.
findings.scenario: Under write contention a new card skips its learning step, and an extra log row counts against the cap.
findings.fix: Ignore e.repeat, isComposing and modifier keys. Add a busy ref with try/finally in grade() and act(). Optionally add an Undo for resolve.

findings.title: Invalid settings values and other input errors become HTTP 500 (or a silent typo success on the CLI), and the Settings page swallows the failure
findings.evidence: Settings(**merged) raises an uncaught ValidationError, so a remotes entry missing host returns 500. fromisoformat(since) and the data-dir body behave the same way. patch() has no catch and saveRemotes doesn't await it. An empty number field sends 0. A mistyped CLI key prints success and saves nothing.
findings.scenario: The user pastes a remotes JSON with a typo and clicks Save: no message, and `rhz sync` later fails.
findings.fix: Use typed SettingsPatch fields (list[RemoteTarget], Literals), catch ValidationError and return 422 with errors(). Type `since` as datetime. Validate CLI keys against model_fields. Make patch() async with an errorText notice, and ignore empty or NaN number values. Add Field(ge=0) constraints.

findings.title: Non-UTF-8 (GBK/UTF-16) exports and folder drops fail opaquely: the inbox writes a traceback report, drag-drop returns 500, and the drop zone crashes silently and allows a concurrent re-drop
findings.evidence: `.decode('utf-8-sig')` has no guard. The sniff uses errors='replace' and then strict decoding fails. A UTF-16 file with a non-RXF suffix is skipped at INFO. f.slice().text() sits outside the try, and there is no busy state.
findings.scenario: A file saved as GBK on Chinese Windows shows 'Internal Server Error', and the report advises pasting it into the chat, which can't fix encoding. Dragging the Downloads folder does nothing.
findings.fix: Add a decode_rxf helper used by every path: honour the BOM, try UTF-8, and fail with a localised 'save as UTF-8' message (gb18030 only with a warning when CJK is clearly present). Return 422 with {report}. Guard the sniff, add a busy state with 'n/N imported', and ignore drops while busy.

findings.title: useLoad keeps the previous page's data when deps change, so entity-to-entity navigation briefly shows the wrong card
findings.evidence: Data is not cleared, and the loader shows only when !c.
findings.scenario: For a moment after clicking, the old title and edges remain.
findings.fix: Render `<EntityPage key={id}>`, which also resets the hops and status state.

findings.title: No live refresh: inbox and MCP ingests and queue changes stay invisible until the user navigates
findings.evidence: Stats are fetched only on route change, and the badge never updates after resolve.
findings.scenario: After resolving 20 items the badge still says 37.
findings.fix: Add useRefreshOnFocus (visibilitychange and focus) plus an 'rhz:stats' event dispatched after mutations.

findings.title: Confirm or reject on an edge updates the buttons but not the row's strike-through, pill or graph
findings.evidence: Local useState(e.status) is used, while the row and pill read the prop.
findings.scenario: The user can't tell whether the reject took effect.
findings.fix: Remove the local state and pass an onChanged callback that reloads the card and graph. Disable the button while a request is in flight and catch errors.

findings.title: Recall has no busy or error state, and the server silently uses only the first 4,000 characters
findings.evidence: There is no catch or disabled state, and no notice of truncation.
findings.scenario: The user double-clicks, waits and gets results for the preamble only.
findings.fix: Add a busy state, catch errors into a notice, and show a character counter with the 4,000 note.

findings.title: Contrast and keyboard-access gaps, including a 1.9:1 queue badge in dark mode
findings.evidence: .nav-count uses #fff on #f0b35a in dark mode. --muted is 3.9:1. Queue rows and the drop label cannot be focused.
findings.scenario: The review count is unreadable in dark mode.
findings.fix: Use a dark text token for the badge, darken --muted, and make the rows and drop label focusable with Enter handlers.

findings.title: Under `rhz serve`, index.html is served without Cache-Control on a fixed port, so a stale shell 404s the new chunks after an upgrade
findings.evidence: Heuristic freshness applies to a plain FileResponse.
findings.scenario: After `pip install -U` the browser tab is blank until a hard reload.
findings.fix: Send Cache-Control: no-cache on the index and SPA routes, immutable on /assets, plus a reload-once handler for vite:preloadError.

findings.title: An absolute or relative inbox_dir crashes the app, CLI and MCP when its parent can't be created, and relative paths resolve against CWD
findings.evidence: ensure_dirs runs mkdir on the inbox with no catch. Verified FileNotFoundError at create_app and `rhz search`. A relative value lands under the install's server dir. The watcher captures the path once while the handler re-reads settings.
findings.scenario: On a new PC without D:, or with the inbox drive unplugged, the sidecar never starts and MCP fails.
findings.fix: Split core dirs from inbox dirs. Make inbox mkdir non-fatal: record inbox_error and fall back or disable the watcher without rewriting settings. LocalClient creates only core dirs. Validate on write (absolute, creatable), show a banner with a 'reset to default' action, and note that a restart is required.

findings.title: `rhz sync` opens three separate SSH sessions (three 2FA prompts) with no timeout, relies on ControlMaster, which Windows OpenSSH lacks, and leaves the scp target unquoted
findings.evidence: The run is ssh mkdir, then scp to .uploading, then ssh mv, each with check=True and no timeout. control_path is the documented 2FA answer but is unsupported on Win32-OpenSSH. _rq('~') quotes to a literal '~'. scp quoting differs between the legacy and SFTP protocols. CalledProcessError is uncaught.
findings.scenario: From Windows to a Duo-protected cluster, each sync asks for password plus Duo three times, and a missed push leaves a traceback.
findings.fix: Use a single `ssh host 'umask 077 && mkdir -p DIR && cat > TMP && chmod 600 TMP && mv -f TMP FINAL'` with the snapshot streamed on stdin, with a timeout. Map '~' to "$HOME". Catch errors and print a localised message naming the step. Warn on win32 when control_path is set. Add tests on the command strings.

findings.title: The global --snapshot option is silently ignored by rebuild, nightly, review, vocab, bench, diag, backup, watch, `ingest --move` and serve
findings.evidence: Only _client() honours the snapshot. Other commands run init_db and session_scope on the default dir, creating it.
findings.scenario: `rhz --snapshot backup.db rebuild`, run to inspect an old copy, rebuilds the live library. vocab and diag on HPC export an empty junk library.
findings.fix: Add _require_writable() to the write commands, which exits 2 in snapshot mode. Add _local_session(), which opens a read-only session on snapshot_settings(path) with no init_db, for vocab, bench and diag. Add a test that the tmp data dir stays empty and the snapshot is untouched.

findings.title: Without RHIZOME_SNAPSHOT or --snapshot, remote rhz silently creates and searches an empty new library, and nothing tells the user to set it
findings.evidence: Reproduced: `env -i HOME=$R rhz search GRN` printed 'No results.' with rc=0 and created ~/.local/share/rhizome. RHIZOME_SNAPSHOT is documented nowhere.
findings.scenario: A job script runs `rhz recall --from-file analysis.py`, gets 'No results', and the user concludes their library has nothing relevant.
findings.fix: Have read commands use LocalClient(create=False) and error with a 'pass --snapshot or export RHIZOME_SNAPSHOT' message (exit 2) when there is no DB. Have sync print the export line. Document it in the README. Optionally name the library and its work count on 'No results'.

findings.title: recall crashes with KeyError 'relevance' on empty or whitespace context, notebooks, and scripts with no imports or comments
findings.evidence: A blank query goes to browse(), whose hits come from summarize() and have no relevance key. context_from_code never parses .ipynb JSON and drops std-only imports. The CLI shows a traceback, the API a 500, MCP an isError.
findings.scenario: On HPC via Jupyter, `rhz recall --from-file analysis.ipynb` gives a traceback: the headline 'writing code on HPC' feature fails on the most common file type.
findings.fix: Return [] early on blank context. Have summarize always emit relevance: None. Parse notebook cells (code plus markdown) and drop #SBATCH/#PBS lines. Have the CLI print no_results when the context is empty. Add tests.

findings.title: POST /decision, DELETE /decision/{id} and POST /topic are not idempotent: repeats duplicate audit rows and queue extra full rebuilds
findings.evidence: Some ops always return True, revoke doesn't check revoked_at, and DELETE always enqueues a rebuild.
findings.scenario: A double DELETE runs two full rebuilds. A twin add_alias survives revoking 'the' decision.
findings.fix: Make revoke a no-op when already revoked, enqueue only when something changed, and use enqueue_once. In record(), skip only when the newest unrevoked decision is identical. On revoke, also revoke identical twins.

findings.title: rhz_ingest has no repair parameter, yet its report tells the user to click 'Repair and import' or run `rhz ingest --repair claude-desktop.yaml`, neither of which exists
findings.evidence: The file is never written to disk on the MCP path.
findings.scenario: Claude passes the bogus advice on to the user, or hand-rewrites the YAML and loses the drift record in L0.
findings.fix: Add repair: bool to rhz_ingest. For MCP, replace the repairable line with 'resubmit with repair=true'. Return the repairable and repairs codes. Add an INSTRUCTIONS line and a test.

findings.title: Filter and pagination parity gaps across API, CLI and MCP, and /decisions has no upper cap
findings.evidence: rhz_search lacks year_max, edge_type, topic, tier and offset. `rhz queue` has no --offset.
findings.scenario: Claude can't narrow a search by year range or topic.
findings.fix: Add the missing parameters (the clients already forward **filters), add --offset, and cap /decisions with a total.

findings.title: There is no version compatibility check between clients and the server
findings.evidence: connect ignores /health.version.
findings.scenario: A dev `rhz` talks to the installed app and fails with a confusing 422 or KeyError.
findings.fix: Warn on stderr when the versions differ. Optionally disable the docs routes in frozen builds.

findings.title: POST /topic and `rhz topic` accept an empty or whitespace name and create topic 'topic:'
findings.evidence: Verified: an empty name returns 200 with key 'topic:'.
findings.scenario: An unnamed topic retro-tags the library against an empty definition.
findings.fix: In decisions._validate, require non-empty text fields per op, and map DecisionError to 422 in /topic.

findings.title: Re-ingesting the same RXF with a PDF attached silently drops the PDF
findings.evidence: The sha-duplicate short-circuit returns before rawstore.put(pdf).
findings.scenario: The user saves via Claude, then drops the same export plus its PDF, and nothing is attached.
findings.fix: In the duplicate branch, store the PDF, append it to a new input_hashes list, and return pdf_attached or pdf_ignored.

findings.title: /ingest has no size or type guard, so any bytes are stored as a PDF
findings.evidence: There is no magic-number check, and stored files are content-addressed permanently.
findings.scenario: A zip renamed to .pdf is stored for good.
findings.fix: Check for b'%PDF-' and a generous size cap in ingest_text, and return a localised failure.

findings.title: create_app is a ~390-line closure, so routes can't be imported and auth or db can't be overridden
findings.evidence: auth compares against a captured local value, and app.state.token is set only at the end.
findings.scenario: Unit-testing a single handler is awkward.
findings.fix: Move auth, writable and db to module level, reading app.state. Split into routers later.

findings.title: There is no way to produce migration 0002, and autogenerate would drop the FTS tables
findings.evidence: Config is built in code. pyproject lists an alembic.ini that doesn't exist. env.py has no include_object filter, so autogenerate proposes 6 remove_table ops for entity_fts*.
findings.scenario: The first autogenerated 0002 drops every user's search index.
findings.fix: Add an include_object filter excluding entity_fts*, a drift test using compare_metadata, and a dev `rhz db revision` or script targeting a scratch DB. Remove the alembic.ini package-data entry.

findings.title: Docs and release metadata disagree with what ships: MSI vs NSIS, 13 vs 14 edges, branch-specific release links, and the version in seven files with no consistency check
findings.evidence: The release tag reads tauri.conf.json, while /health, diag and the User-Agent read __init__.py.
findings.scenario: A release tagged v0.1.3 reports 0.1.2 in diag, and the README link 404s once the branch is gone.
findings.fix: Fix the docs. Add scripts/check_version.py to CI and assert /health.version against tauri.conf in release. Use tag-relative links.

findings.title: The entity, edge and review-kind vocabularies are hand-copied in 10+ places across backend, frontend and docs
findings.evidence: All copies match today, but adding relates_to touched 9 files.
findings.scenario: A new edge type is missing from the legend, the filters and i18n.
findings.fix: Import ASSET_TYPES in the backend. Add a pytest that regex-checks the frontend lists and i18n keys against models. Remove the hard-coded counts from docs.

findings.title: The installer ships OFL fonts and ~49 frozen Python packages (plus Rust crates) with no third-party notices
findings.evidence: NOTICE covers only models, which aren't shipped.
findings.scenario: The first external tester's install folder lacks the required attributions.
findings.fix: Add scripts/gen_third_party_notices.py (pip-licenses, license-checker, cargo about) called from release, and bundle THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.

findings.title: Dead code and inconsistencies: unused i18n keys, two MCP entry points with different bootstrap, Graph.clock as a bare mutable attribute, deprecated utcnow
findings.evidence: rhizome-mcp skips setup_logging and RHIZOME_SNAPSHOT.
findings.scenario: A pip user's MCP leaves no log.
findings.fix: Share one bootstrap, use a Graph.at() context manager, use the models.utcnow helper, and delete the unused keys.

findings.title: The RXF export instructions, skeleton and vocab can't be reached from the installed app's UI or from the MCP server, though step 1 of capture depends on them
findings.evidence: Home tells the user to put the instructions in a Project, but no screen or endpoint serves them, and `rhz` isn't on PATH. MCP INSTRUCTIONS assume a Project and expose no tool, resource or prompt with the skeleton or vocab.
findings.scenario: A new user, or any plain Claude Desktop chat, produces invented YAML. Every file lands in error/, rhz_ingest loops several times, and topics ignore the vocab.
findings.fix: Add GET /rxf/instructions?lang and a Settings 'Chat Project setup' panel (copy instructions, download md and vocab) linked from home.step1. Add an MCP tool rhz_rxf_guide() returning the instructions plus the current vocab, and have INSTRUCTIONS say to call it unless the Project already has it. Also add a resource and prompt. Add a first-run section to the README.

findings.title: Error-report hints tell the LLM to delete misplaced asset lists and leave out allowed values, which loses data and costs extra rounds
findings.evidence: A top-level `datasets:` gives 'remove datasets'. claims.*.claim and paper.journal give 'remove'. A missing enum gives 'add relation' with no values. A list item of the wrong type has an empty field name.
findings.scenario: Claude obeys 'remove datasets', and the paper ingests with no dataset assets.
findings.fix: Extend _KNOWN with move and rename hints (assets:, text, q/a, venue). Add enum values from the schema. Name the list and print the item's required keys. Append the compact skeleton when there are many causes.

findings.title: A missing required field is reported N×N times, so the place counts are wrong
findings.evidence: Each 'required' error is expanded over the whole validator_value list.
findings.scenario: The report says '(2 places)' for a single claim.
findings.fix: Emit only the key named by each error, or dedupe (path, kind, field). Add a test.

findings.title: The vocab export leaves out candidate topics, so the Project vocab is nearly empty for weeks
findings.evidence: Only active topics are included, while new topics start as candidates. Neither the UI nor the CLI can pass include_candidates.
findings.scenario: The chat keeps inventing new phrasings and topics fragment.
findings.fix: By default include candidates with at least 1 work in a separate candidate_topics section marked with status and work count, and tell the chat to prefer active topics. Add a UI and CLI toggle.

findings.title: Nothing tells the user when rhizome-vocab.yaml in the Project is out of date
findings.evidence: No export time or hash is recorded.
findings.scenario: New topics are missing from the chat for weeks.
findings.fix: On download, record vocab_exported_at plus a body hash, compute a vocab_stale flag in /stats, and show a hint.

findings.title: Any prose before or after the YAML code block makes the whole file fail, with a report that points at a backtick
findings.evidence: _FENCE is anchored to the whole text, while the detectors accept a fence anywhere.
findings.scenario: The user copies the whole message, including the model's closing sentence, and it lands in error/ repeatedly.
findings.fix: Extract the first fenced block (``` or ~~~, any info string) whose body has rxf_version at the start of a line. Add tests.

findings.title: The skeleton's fixed 'deep-review-v2' prompt_version is copied verbatim by LLMs, and depth defaults to deep
findings.evidence: The field is only displayed. Depth affects the tier when a PDF is present.
findings.scenario: Old and new exports can't be told apart after the instructions change.
findings.fix: Put an instructions version in the header with a 'copy as is' note, add a light/deep criterion, and add a contract test.

findings.title: A user insight that auto-merges into a model idea turns the model's idea into a 'yours' idea and loses the user's wording
findings.evidence: update_attrs(origin='user', weight=2.0) is applied to whatever resolve_free returns. Reproduced.
findings.scenario: Paper M's model idea shows the 'yours' pill with ×2 recall weight and priority 10, while the user's sentence survives only as an alias.
findings.fix: Pass origin into resolve_free and downgrade cross-origin auto-merges to a queued merge item. Upgrade origin only when the entity was created or is already a user idea. When a cross-origin merge is accepted, the user entity survives. Add tests.

findings.title: The T2 tier is never recorded on the Work: a deep export with a PDF still shows T1 and tier=2 search never matches
findings.evidence: `w.tier = max(w.tier, 1)` ignores ex.tier. Reproduced.
findings.scenario: The paper card shows T1 and the tier filter returns nothing.
findings.fix: Use `max(w.tier, ex.tier or 1)`. Add a test covering ingest and rebuild.

findings.title: NLI 'also_supports' always writes a supports edge, even when the paper's stance is contradicts, and contradiction items carry no stance
findings.evidence: There is no check on c.stance. Accepting a contradiction item always writes a contradicts edge.
findings.scenario: Once NLI is enabled, a rebuttal paper is listed as evidence FOR the claim it rejects.
findings.fix: Propagate also_supports only when stance is supports. Put stance in the contradiction payload and invert the accepted edge when the stance is contradicts. Add tests.

findings.title: Free-concept attributes from later exports are silently dropped (method io and biotools, idea transfer, fields of datasets without an accession)
findings.evidence: resolve_free returns early on alias, key or auto-merge hits without applying attrs. Reproduced: ArchR keeps only {name}, so the io card is never made and io never enters the FTS or embedding text.
findings.scenario: Popular tools first seen in light exports stay thin forever, which hurts search and cards on a 5k library.
findings.fix: Add Graph.fill_attrs that fills only missing keys, call it on every created=False path in resolve_free with per-type mergeable keys, and reindex on change. Keep per-paper transfer on edges. Add a regression test and a rematerialise note.

findings.title: applicable_to transfer attrs on a shared idea are overwritten by the last paper while the edge keeps the first paper's extraction_id
findings.evidence: upsert_edge merges attrs with last-wins and keeps extraction_id with first-wins. Nothing reads these edge attrs.
findings.scenario: The raw edge JSON in MCP contradicts the asset card.
findings.fix: Stop writing transfer attrs on the edge, or append per-extraction records.

findings.title: upsert_edge mixes provenance between exports: a light→deep upgrade or a work merge leaves evidence from one export, attrs from another and confidence from max()
findings.evidence: Reproduced: evidence 'Fig 1 (light)' with extraction_id=1, deep attrs (logic_jump) and confidence 1.0. Merging works drops the merged-away evidence.
findings.scenario: Upgrading a paper from light to deep, the documented path, leaves incoherent claim edges, and the logic-jump confidence of 0.5 is lost.
findings.fix: When a different extraction_id arrives, replace evidence, extraction_id, confidence and attrs as one record and append the old values to attrs.evidence_records. Use the same helper in merge(). Keep max() for writes within one extraction. Add tests.

findings.title: A later light export overwrites the deep export's tldr on the Work
findings.evidence: update_attrs replaces values. Reproduced.
findings.scenario: Search uses the one-line light summary.
findings.fix: Overwrite tldr only from an export at least as deep. Fill OpenAlex authors and venue only when missing.

findings.title: When several papers cite the same dataset or method, entity attrs (tissue, organism, scale, ...) are last-writer-wins
findings.evidence: update_attrs overwrites on existing accessions. Reproduced: tissue='shoot' from the last user paper.
findings.scenario: The producing paper's description is overwritten by whichever user paper was ingested last.
findings.fix: Add merge_reported_attrs: fill when empty, let the producer (produces/proposes) be authoritative, and record conflicts in attrs.reported. Apply on both the create and update paths. Add order tests.

findings.title: File-local item ids (t2, d1, m1) leak into entity attrs and are shown: idea transfer.to, and an 'id' row on datasets and methods
findings.evidence: The instructions require ids such as `to: t2`, and they are stored raw. Cards read 'cross-modality → t2' and the FTS text gets 't2'. update_attrs overwrites the id.
findings.scenario: Most deep exports with a transfer idea show meaningless ids to the user and to Claude.
findings.fix: Resolve transfer.to via lookup to a canonical name and to_key (drop the raw id), and update existing ideas. Exclude 'id' from dataset and method attrs. Backfill and reindex once.

findings.title: edit_text on a user insight doesn't change what the paper card and rhz_get show, and no UI, CLI or MCP path can issue it
findings.evidence: The insights come from the immutable Extraction.output. The design promises 可以在论文卡片里修改.
findings.scenario: The corrected wording appears only on the idea page, and Claude keeps quoting the model's paraphrase.
findings.fix: Record insight→entity keys in ex.meta during materialisation, falling back to user proposes edges. In entity_card, emit canonical_name plus original_text. Add a pencil-edit button that calls edit_text, and a CLI/MCP equivalent.

findings.title: Accepting a contradiction review puts the evidence in attrs rather than the edge column, with no evidence_type, strength or extraction id
findings.evidence: Reproduced: evidence column is None, attrs={'evidence','origin': 'user'}.
findings.scenario: Accepted contradicts edges show no location or strength, and source_works returns None.
findings.fix: Carry evidence_type, strength and extraction_id in the payload. Let add_edge accept evidence and extraction_id and pass them to upsert_edge.

findings.title: 'Useful' synthesis pairs and manual create_idea produce orphan Ideas: edges are made only to topics, and no card is created
findings.evidence: Synthesis pairs are always assets, so 0 edges are created. Reproduced. Links are stored only in hidden attrs, the text is 'A ↔ B', and the orphan sits close to both assets, so next week's synthesis re-proposes it.
findings.scenario: Every pair the user endorses is lost from the graph and fed back as noise.
findings.fix: Create confirmed relates_to edges (origin=user) to non-topic links, as materialize.py:224 does, and keep links_unresolved separately. Validate keys on live record only. Create a priority-10 user-idea card. Add a note field to Digest. Backfill via rebuild replay.

findings.title: A review card about a rejected (fabricated) accession attaches to the paper, and the insight's link to it is dropped silently
findings.evidence: `target or work` is used, and links_unresolved is hidden.
findings.scenario: A Q/A about GSE-FAKE-1 enters FSRS.
findings.fix: Skip cards whose about-item was rejected, and show links_unresolved.

findings.title: Claim entity attrs keep the first paper's evidence_type and boundary as properties of the claim, and per-paper edge attrs are not shown
findings.evidence: AssetAttrs shows 'Evidence type: causal'.
findings.scenario: The claim page shows evidence quality from one paper as fact.
findings.fix: Hide those attrs on claims. Render edge evidence_type, boundary and logic_jump in EdgeGroups.

findings.title: bio.tools ids are parsed but never used as anchors
findings.evidence: Only repo anchors. Reproduced: two ArchR entities.
findings.scenario: Methods without a repo don't align across papers.
findings.fix: Normalise the bt id, add a biotools:<id> alias everywhere, and look it up in both branches.

findings.title: The paper card never shows the OpenAlex abstract, authors, links or paper types, or issue locations
findings.evidence: The attrs and the locale keys exist but are unused.
findings.scenario: An issue appears without its figure reference.
findings.fix: Render the abstract (collapsible), authors, DOI/OA links, type pills and x.location.

findings.title: Decision history, revoke and direct correction ops (merge, split, rename, alias, edit_text, add_edge, create_idea) have no UI, CLI or MCP surface
findings.evidence: GET /decisions and DELETE /decision exist but have no caller. The UI reaches only edge_status and confirm_topic. Silent auto-merges (≥0.9) never create queue items. The docs mark undo ✅.
findings.scenario: The user wants to undo last week's merge or split a false auto-merge. The only way is curl with the token.
findings.fix: Add Client decisions() and revoke(), plus `rhz decisions`, `rhz undo ID` and typed `rhz rename/alias/merge/split/link/idea`. Add MCP rhz_edit and rhz_undo, gated on confirmation. In the UI, add a Decisions history page with Undo that polls the rebuild job, and an Edit menu on entities (rename, alias, merge-into picker, split, link). Show aliases with their source.

findings.title: Revoking a merge of two papers leaves the merged paper's exports, cards and raw objects attached to the other paper
findings.evidence: merge rewrites Extraction.work_key and RawObject.work_key, and rebuild never re-stamps them. Verified: after revoke and rebuild, W2 has 0 exports and W1 has 2.
findings.scenario: An accidental merge followed by undo shows B's TL;DR and insights as A's, permanently.
findings.fix: In rebuild pass 1, set ex.work_key and RawObject.work_key from each materialise result before apply_all replays the active merges. Add a test. Accept or document that ReviewCard origin is lost.

findings.title: split leaves the alias on the original entity (so the next paper re-merges into it), never records the pair as distinct, and always reports success even when no edge matched
findings.evidence: No alias is removed, and edge mismatches `continue`, then `return True`. The op is reachable only through a raw POST.
findings.scenario: A hand-typed split creates an orphan duplicate, or is undone by the next ingest.
findings.fix: Resolve the edges first and raise or return False when none match, before creating anything. Move the matching aliases. Record a distinct pair and have auto-merge consult distinct_pairs.

findings.title: After a revoke, the revoked merge or distinct pair never comes back to the review queue
findings.evidence: dedupe_key is unique in every status, and rebuild deletes only pending items.
findings.scenario: The user revokes a merge to re-decide it as is_a, and the question never reappears.
findings.fix: In revoke(), delete the non-pending merge and topic_relation items for that pair so the rebuild re-queues them. Add a test.

findings.title: Decision keys are case- and format-sensitive and errors give no hints; a mistyped create_topic parent is silently dropped
findings.evidence: The errors are a bare 'not found' or 'had no effect'.
findings.scenario: A Chinese display name typed as a key fails with no suggestion.
findings.fix: In record(), resolve by alias and canonicalise the payload. Validate the parent. List EDGE_TYPES in the error. Suggest 'did you mean' keys. Use a topic picker in Map.

findings.title: The zh/en alias language has no visible effect: display never prefers the alias in the UI language
findings.evidence: Only canonical_name is emitted.
findings.scenario: Adding a Chinese alias changes nothing in the zh_CN UI.
findings.fix: Return a names {lang: alias} map built in one query, and have a frontend displayName() pick by i18n.language.

findings.title: There is no op to discard a bogus candidate topic, and topics with 3 or more works auto-promote
findings.evidence: Only confirm_topic exists.
findings.scenario: 'benchmarking' lands on the map and stays in search.
findings.fix: Add a replayed reject_topic op, exclude rejected topics in the search, vocab and recall readers, and add Reject and 'Merge into…' buttons.

findings.title: Re-ingesting raw/ doesn't reproduce the library: PDF pairing, OpenAlex responses, filenames and timestamps exist only in the DB
findings.evidence: Nothing in raw/ links a PDF to its YAML. OpenAlex is only in L1, so offline replay gives different keys and created_at resets.
findings.scenario: After a DB loss, deep papers come back as tier 1 with no PDF, and the timeline is reset.
findings.fix: Store OpenAlex JSON as an L0 object. Write a write-once <sha>.meta.json (filename, captured_at, pdf_sha, openalex_sha, repairs). Add `rhz recover --from-raw` that replays in captured_at order with stored responses. Pair with D5.

findings.title: No bulk export of the graph, insights, decisions or cards in an open format, and scripting /entity skews the forgetting signal
findings.evidence: Raw YAML exists, but FSRS state and decisions are SQLite-only.
findings.scenario: Building a paper appendix or moving to Anki or Obsidian means reverse-engineering the schema.
findings.fix: Add `rhz export -o DIR` (read-only session) producing key-based JSONL for entities, edges, decisions and cards plus a PDF index. Add touch=false to the /entity query.

findings.title: Switching from SQLite to Postgres has no data-copy path, the desktop build can't load psycopg, and Postgres silently skips every safety backup
findings.evidence: backup_database returns None on non-SQLite, and the log says 'backed up to None'.
findings.scenario: A rebuild on Postgres deletes with no backup.
findings.fix: On Postgres, write a SQLite snapshot as the backup (or warn). Show a clear message in the desktop build. Document that switching starts empty.

findings.title: raw/ can't be placed or synced separately, and nothing verifies its integrity
findings.evidence: read() returns None silently, and there is no check.
findings.scenario: Cloud placeholders mean L0 is missing at exactly the moment it's needed.
findings.fix: Add a backup_target mirror (copy-if-absent for raw/ plus rotated DB copies) and `rhz check` for missing or mismatched raw files. Log a warning on a missing read.

findings.title: The nightly job (communities, promotion, weekly synthesis) is scheduled only after 30 uninterrupted idle minutes, so short desktop sessions never produce a digest
findings.evidence: maybe_schedule_nightly fires only at idle ticks%900==0, and ticks reset each start. The manual button sends {}, so the 7-day guard skips synthesis, and the page reloads after 1.5 s. Assets from weeks with no run are never synthesised.
findings.scenario: The researcher uses Rhizome in 10-20 minute sessions on a sleeping laptop. Communities never compute, topics stay candidates, and the Digest stays empty.
findings.fix: Check for nightly at worker start and every ~5 minutes by wall clock. Use a catch-up synthesis window (since=last_synthesis). Add a force_synthesis payload and poll the job to completion on Digest. Show the last batch time.

findings.title: The synthesis feedback threshold ratchets to 0.95, then overrides the configured value for good and is shared across embedders
findings.evidence: A ±0.01 step means mostly-useless cross-field pairs drive it upward, KV takes precedence over settings, and there is no reset.
findings.scenario: Within about a month the digest is permanently empty, and changing the setting does nothing.
findings.fix: Store a clamped delta per embedder (±0.15) over the live setting, use a target-rate step (T=0.2), guard against missing values, add a reset command or endpoint, and show the threshold in Digest.

findings.title: Claude's rhz_get calls count as the user 'seeing' an asset and suppress what recall just surfaced
findings.evidence: Reproduced: scores drop from 0.35 to 0.19 after entity_card on the top hits.
findings.scenario: For weeks, forgetting measures Claude's tool traffic rather than the user's memory.
findings.fix: Add touch: bool to the Client get methods and a ?touch=false query on /entity. Have rhz_get pass False. Add a test covering both paths.

findings.title: There is no way to suspend or delete a bad card, and cards for rejected entities stay due
findings.evidence: suspend() has no caller, and 's' in the CLI only skips for the session.
findings.scenario: Wrong LLM or template cards and cards about hallucinated datasets have to be graded forever.
findings.fix: Add POST /cards/{id}/suspend with an 's' key and button. Add an entity-level no_cards flag honoured by _make_cards. Filter cards with no non-rejected source edge in due_cards at query time.

findings.title: Cards generated by the local LLM lose the user-Idea priority
findings.evidence: No priority is passed on the local_llm branch.
findings.scenario: With a local LLM, the user's ideas sit among hundreds of new cards.
findings.fix: Compute prio once and pass it to all three upsert_card calls. Add a test.

findings.title: Template idea cards repeat one title-only question for every idea of a paper
findings.evidence: q depends only on the title, and entity_name (the answer) is shown before reveal.
findings.scenario: A deep export with 5 ideas produces 5 identical priority-10 questions whose answers are visible up front.
findings.fix: Build the question from transfer.to or the linked assets. Aggregate or skip ideas with no cue. Hide entity_name before reveal for template cards. Re-key existing cards (keeping their history) and add a test.

findings.title: The Home 'cards due' count ignores the daily caps
findings.evidence: Every unintroduced card is counted.
findings.scenario: Home says 1,742 due, while the Cards page shows 20 and then done.
findings.fix: Return the capped number due_cards would serve, and optionally show the backlog separately.

findings.title: The dispute list shows only contradicts edges created in the last 7 days, with no read state
findings.evidence: It is a rolling window, and the UI can't change days.
findings.scenario: After a holiday, the new contradictions never appear.
findings.fix: Add a KV digest_ack_at set by an explicit 'mark read' action, with since=min(now-7d, ack). Optionally add a days selector.

findings.title: Ingest-time related-papers ranking ignores forgetting, has no hub damping, counts duplicate edges and includes rejected edges
findings.evidence: A flat +0.5 per shared row, and an unfiltered inner subquery.
findings.scenario: Papers sharing a broad topic and Seurat outrank a strong semantic match.
findings.fix: Filter rejected edges, count each shared entity once with a 1/log(2+degree) weight, keep the best semantic match per dimension, apply forgetting, and break ties deterministically.

findings.title: The Cards page drops FSRS learning steps: 'Again' cards due in minutes vanish until the page is reopened
findings.evidence: Cards are reloaded with due<=now right after the last grade.
findings.scenario: Failed cards never get repeated within the session.
findings.fix: Keep graded cards that are due within ~30 minutes in a local pending list and show a countdown before 'done'.

findings.title: requires-python >=3.11 blocks the common Python 3.10 cluster modules even though the code runs on 3.10, and there is no offline install path
findings.evidence: All 106 tests pass on 3.10. Only .exe files are published.
findings.scenario: `module load python/3.10` followed by pip install fails, and the remote side can't be installed.
findings.fix: Set >=3.10 and add a 3.10 CI job. Document pipx/uv, a conda 3.11 environment, and an offline wheelhouse. Optionally publish the wheel.

findings.title: Snapshot mode discards user settings: --lang, the remote settings.json, thresholds and the embedder
findings.evidence: A new Settings(data_dir=snapshot.parent) replaces the resolved one. Reproduced: --lang zh_CN prints English. The vector filter mismatches when the desktop used bge-m3.
findings.scenario: On a cluster without zh locales the output is English, and vector recall is silently off.
findings.fix: Use get_settings().model_copy(update={'database_url': ...}). Warn when the snapshot's Embedding models don't include the current embedder. Add a test.

findings.title: The synced snapshot lands world-readable on a shared cluster
findings.evidence: There is no umask or chmod, so mode is 644 under the typical 022 umask, and the file contains the whole library, including personal ideas.
findings.scenario: Other users on a Palmetto-style cluster can sqlite3 the researcher's unpublished notes.
findings.fix: Run umask 077 and create the tmp file before upload, then chmod 600 before mv. Don't chmod existing parent dirs. Add a README note and a command-string test.

findings.title: Download hints give wrong commands for project and study accessions and never use ENA or Zenodo
findings.evidence: PRJNA gets `prefetch X && fasterq-dump X`, and Zenodo falls through to 'Search'.
findings.scenario: A job script fails at fasterq-dump.
findings.fix: Classify runs vs projects inside download_hint, add an ENA filereport URL, Zenodo and the GEO FTP suppl path, update both .po files, and add a parametrised test.

findings.title: The remote can't tell how stale its snapshot is
findings.evidence: No metadata is written.
findings.scenario: Weeks-old snapshots silently miss new papers.
findings.fix: Write kv snapshot_meta {created_at, version, head} into the copy, and print a stderr warning when it is older than about 7 days.

findings.title: Terminal output truncates by character count (CJK is double width), and `rhz get` and rhz_get accept only an id or internal key
findings.evidence: `[:60]` slicing is used, and only by_key lookups are made.
findings.scenario: Chinese lines wrap, and a pasted DOI or accession returns 'not found'.
findings.fix: Add an east-asian-width-aware _clip. Add a server-side resolve_ref (key, then DOI, then external id or alias, then candidates) behind /entity/by-key.

refuted.title: Store (MSIX) Claude Desktop: `rhz.exe mcp` inherits package identity, so local-mode writes to %APPDATA%\Rhizome are redirected to a per-package shadow copy
refuted.why: The code references are accurate. system.py:122-132 does look for the MSIX config under Packages\Claude_*\LocalCache\Roaming\Claude. config.py:22-24 makes %APPDATA%\Rhizome the default library. client.py:291 falls back to a read-write LocalClient(st) when no server is reachable. The finding's central mechanism is still wrong. It says that on the first write SQLite copy-on-writes rhizome.db into the package's LocalCache and edits the copy there, so the desktop app never sees the change. That is not how MSIX AppData virtualization is documented to work on Windows 10 1903 and later. Only newly created files and folders under AppData go to the private per-package location. Changes to files that already exist in the real AppData are allowed and land in the real file. Claude's own config ends up in LocalCache because Claude created it as a new file, which fits that rule and is no evidence of copy-on-write. By the time the user clicks 'Connect to Claude Desktop' inside the Rhizome app, the app's backend has already created %APPDATA%\Rhizome\rhizome.db, so writes to the existing database file go to the real location. Two further points are unverified: whether the spawned rhz.exe really inherits package identity, and whether Claude's manifest disables write virtualization. The finding admits it was never checked on a Store install. With the main 'shadow copy of the DB' claim contradicted by the platform's documented behaviour, I cannot confirm the scenario as stated.

refuted.title: Local LLM path: 2048-token context with 1500-char abstracts, and model errors propagate into ingest and retro jobs
refuted.why:
Parts of the claim are accurate, but the failure scenario it describes is not reachable as stated. I checked these in the code:

(1) Ingest path. `_make_cards` (materialize.py:321-339) only calls `backend.make_card` on `out.assets`. That list holds claims, datasets, methods and ideas (lines 164/176/189/203/213), and claims are skipped at line 331. The work entity is never in it. So `_card_context` only ever renders short `entity_text` for a dataset, method or idea, plus the work title (graph.py:47-53), and never includes the 1500-char abstract. A context overflow cannot make an ingest fail this way.

(2) Retro path. `entity_text` for a work is the title, the tldr and `abstract[:1500]` (graph.py:46), and it is passed together with the topic definition (retro.py:52). Qwen's tokenizer averages about 1.3-1.5 Chinese characters per token, so 1500 Chinese characters come to roughly 1,000-1,200 tokens. The system prompt and definition add about 100-200 tokens. That stays well under the 2048 window. When prompt plus max_tokens would exceed n_ctx, llama-cpp-python shrinks max_tokens instead of failing. It only raises when the prompt alone is at least n_ctx, which needs an unusually long tldr or topic definition. The claimed "one token per character" rate overstates the risk, and even at that rate the total is about 1,850 tokens.

(3) What is true: n_ctx=2048 is set at local_llm.py:20, and neither materialize.py:332 nor retro.py:52 wraps the backend call in try/except. A llama_cpp exception from any cause would therefore propagate. That is a generic robustness point, not the token-overflow failure the finding claims.

refuted.title: `/health` and the Settings page expose no version, schema revision, data path or worker/inbox state, so bug reports lack the basics
refuted.why: The headline claim is wrong on the main points. `/health` already returns the version: app.py:174 returns `{"ok": True, "version": __version__, ...}`, which is the auditor's own quoted evidence. The Settings page does show the data path: Settings.tsx:13 calls `api.system()`, and lines 96-105 render data_dir, inbox, logs and app_dir from system.py:79-96. A diagnostics path also exists already. `rhz diag` (cli.py:423-442) writes a zip with the version, Python, platform, home stats, settings without secrets and every rhizome.log* file, and implementation.zh.md:39 lists this as done. That bundle is what a bug report would use, and the startup error 'could not recover stale jobs' would be in the logs it collects. Parts of the claim do hold: the UI shows no version (`api.health` at api.ts:105 is never called), nothing reports the alembic current/head revision, and nothing reports whether the worker or inbox watcher is alive. That is a small UX gap, not the 'bug reports lack the basics' failure described in the scenario.

refuted.title: Job handlers have no timeout: a hung `sync` (ssh prompting from a windowless process) silently blocks the only worker, and its ssh error text is lost
refuted.why: The code details are accurate, but the scenario can't be reached through the product. backend/rhizome/services/snapshot.py:75 does run `subprocess.run(c, check=True)` with no timeout and no output capture. jobs.py:65-69 stores only str(e) plus the traceback, so the ssh stderr goes to the sidecar log (main.rs:55-57) and never reaches the job error. jobs.Worker (jobs.py:107-133) is one thread with no per-job deadline. recover_stale_jobs only re-queues jobs on restart, and /health (api/app.py:172-174) reports no job state. However, nothing the user uses ever enqueues a `sync` job. The frontend calls runJob only for "nightly" (Digest.tsx:23) and "rebuild" (Settings.tsx:157), and runJob always sends `payload: {}`, which would fail with KeyError on p["remote"] anyway. Settings has no sync button, mcp_server.py has no sync tool, and nightly does not call sync. The real path is `rhz sync` (cli.py:398-410), which calls snapshot.sync directly in the user's terminal. There ssh can prompt for 2FA normally and its stderr shows on screen. Reaching the `sync` job handler (jobs.py:172) takes a hand-written POST /jobs with {"kind":"sync","payload":{"remote":...}}. Also, the sidecar is started with stdin set to null and CREATE_NO_WINDOW (main.rs:55, 67-68), so an ssh password/2FA prompt has no console to read from. It would most likely fail at once with exit 255 instead of hanging for days. A stalled network link (e.g. a laptop that sleeps during scp) could still hang it, but only on that unreached job path.

refuted.title: Timing-dependent subprocess test with a 30 s/15 s budget and no job or test timeout
refuted.why:
The surface facts are right. `deadline = time.time() + 30` and `srv.wait(timeout=15)` are at backend/tests/test_system.py:140/153. The port is picked by bind/close (lines 128-130). `serve` defaults to `watch_inbox=True` (cli.py:72). `watch_parent` polls every 2 s (system.py:240-252). ci.yml has no `timeout-minutes`, and pyproject has no pytest-timeout (only `testpaths`). But both failure scenarios are wrong.

(1) A slow cold start does not turn the build red. When the 30 s connect loop runs out, it just falls through: nothing asserts that the connection succeeded. The next check, `assert srv.poll() is None`, only confirms the child hasn't exited. Also, in cli.py `watch_parent(int(parent))` runs before `create_app(...)`. Only `import uvicorn` and settings come first, so the heavy app, SQLAlchemy and Alembic startup is not on the critical path. Once the parent is killed, the watcher thread calls `os._exit(0)` within about 2 s, even if the app is still initialising. If the watcher hasn't started yet, `pid_alive` is already false on its first check, and it exits 0 straight away. The child would have to fail to even start the watcher within roughly 45 s (30 + 15) for the test to fail.

(2) The "job sits for six hours" scenario can't happen from this test. Every wait is bounded. `srv.wait(timeout=15)` raises TimeoutExpired, and the `finally` block kills both processes. The fake parent sleeps only 60 s.

What remains is a theoretical port race (bind/close, then the child binds). That is rare on a local loopback ephemeral port, and in that case the child exits nonzero and fails fast rather than hanging. Missing job timeouts are a generic hygiene point that this test does not trigger.

refuted.title: Claude Desktop (Store/MSIX build) MCP child sees a virtualized %APPDATA% and silently creates/uses an empty library
refuted.why: The code is quoted correctly. config.py:25 builds the data dir from os.environ['APPDATA']. system.py:145-146 adds RHIZOME_DATA_DIR only when the data dir is not the default. client.py:283/291 falls back to LocalClient when there is no token file. What fails is the premise. MSIX (Store) packaging does not change the APPDATA environment variable. %APPDATA% stays C:\Users\<u>\AppData\Roaming, and that is what rhz.exe inherits. The package uses filesystem virtualization instead. Only files and folders that the packaged process creates new under AppData are redirected to Packages\<pkg>\LocalCache\Roaming. That location is merged into the normal AppData view, and existing files at the real location stay readable and, on Windows 10 1903+, writable. The Rhizome desktop app runs unpackaged and creates %APPDATA%\Rhizome\rhizome.db, the token and location.json at the real location. A child process in Claude's package context therefore sees the real library and token, so connect() takes the HTTP path or opens the real DB. It does not create an empty library. The LocalCache search at system.py:132 also does not show that APPDATA is redirected. It exists because Claude creates its own config file, and a new file is redirected under virtualization. So 'processes it spawns inherit that APPDATA' is factually wrong, and the described silent split into an empty library does not occur in the normal flow, where the app has run before the user clicks 'Connect to Claude Desktop'. I could not test on Windows/MSIX here; this conclusion rests on documented MSIX behaviour. Two parts of the code observation are accurate in isolation: the default install pins nothing, and MCP falls back to a local DB without any check. That leaves only edge cases, for example the MCP server running before any library exists, or a launcher whose APPDATA environment variable really differs. Neither matches the claimed high-severity scenario.

refuted.title: Process-wide singletons need five separate resets, and the in-process vector cache keys every read-only snapshot under the same 'sqlite://' key
refuted.why:
Two of the factual claims are accurate, but neither leads to a failure that can happen today, and the user-facing scenario is false.

What is accurate:
- The globals exist.
- conftest calls the four resets.
- `_VectorCache._key` uses `str(s.get_bind().url)`. A read-only engine is built with `create_engine("sqlite://", creator=...)` (db/session.py:47), so every read-only snapshot gets the key `'sqlite://'`.

Why the snapshot collision cannot happen today: a process only ever opens one snapshot. `connect(snapshot=...)` (client.py:270-275) runs once per CLI or MCP process, with one path from `--snapshot` / `RHIZOME_SNAPSHOT`. No command opens two. The read-write engine has a different key (`sqlite:///path`), so it does not collide with the read-only one. Even if two snapshots did meet, the signature includes `embedding_version` as well as count and id_sum. The collision only shows up in a hypothetical future `rhz compare` command or a hypothetical test.

The Settings/Postgres scenario is false:
1. `SettingsPatch` (api/app.py:103-116) has no `database_url` field. A PATCH cannot change the database at all.
2. Even if it could, `get_engine` and `session_scope` (db/session.py:64-87) key `_engines` / `_makers` by `f"{settings.db_url}|ro=..."` and read the current settings on every call. After `set_settings(new)`, the next request would build and use a new engine. The app would not keep serving the old one; the old engine would just stay in memory unused. So leaving `dispose_all()` out of `patch_settings` is not a correctness bug.

What remains is a general point that test resets are spread across several functions. That is a maintainability opinion, not a defect that would affect this product.

refuted.title: Lint/type baseline is thin: ruff runs E/F only, mypy is not in CI (39 errors, several reachable None derefs), frontend has no linter and carries eslint-disable comments for an absent tool
refuted.why: The tooling facts check out. backend/pyproject.toml has only `[tool.ruff] line-length = 110` with no `select`, and ci.yml:30 runs `ruff check backend`. frontend/package.json has no eslint, yet frontend/src/hooks.ts:21 and :36 carry `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`. api.ts uses `any` at 110/118/132/136. But the finding rests on its "reachable None derefs" and its user-facing scenario, and none of those are reachable. (1) In app.py:252-260, `/entity/by-key` already raises 404 when `Graph(s).by_key(key)` is None. It then calls `entity_card(s, e.id)`, which returns None only when `s.get(Entity, id)` is None (views.py:31-33). That cannot happen in the same session for an entity just loaded, so a 200 with `null` cannot occur. A merged-away or deleted key gets a 404, so the stated scenario is false. (2) POST /topic (app.py:323-325): `_op_create_topic` (decisions.py:181-200) finds or creates the topic by `free_key("topic", name)` or by `by_alias("topic", name)`. The endpoint then looks it up with exactly those two lookups, so `topic` is not None after a successful `record`. (3) decisions.py:167-168, where `upsert_edge` returns None for src==dst: the AttributeError is caught by `apply()` (decisions.py:84-94). Under strict mode (`record`) it becomes a DecisionError, and on replay it is logged and returns False. That is a handled error, not a crash. (4) review.py:53-55 calls `entity_card` only after `e = g.by_key(key)` was checked for None, so the card cannot be None. What is left is a generic note that mypy/eslint are absent, not a product-biting defect.
